overall.assessment: Prema dostavljenoj strukturi — a ne neovisnoj provjeri cjelovitog audiozapisa — podcast prikazuje obraćenje kao put od nasilja, ovisnosti i očaja prema susretu s Kristom, obnovi odnosa, obiteljskom životu i služenju drugima. Takav naglasak snažno odgovara kršćanskoj nadi da Božji poziv dopire i do čovjeka u dubokoj moralnoj i egzistencijalnoj krizi te da se obraćenje očituje u promjeni života, pomirenju i solidarnosti, a ne samo u osjećaju vjere. Struktura također čuva dostojanstvo čovjeka koji je bio ovisan, zatvoren, psihički bolestan ili beskućnik, prikazujući ga kao osobu sposobnu primiti pomoć, obnoviti odnose i pridonijeti dobru drugih. Glavne teološke ograde odnose se na to da se psihičke bolesti i ovisnosti ne svedu na duhovni problem, da se nasilje ne romantizira kao etapa prošlosti te da se osobno svjedočanstvo dopuni jasnoćom o odgovornosti, stručnoj pomoći i širim društvenim uzrocima patnje.
seeds_of_logos: Obraćenje nije prikazano samo kao prekid s prošlošću nego kao preusmjerenje cijelog života prema Bogu, uz plodove u odnosima, obitelji i služenju. Kršćansko obraćenje uključuje promjenu srca, napuštanje grijeha i konkretne plodove pravde i spremnosti na oproštenje.

Motivi pomirenja s ocem i obnavljanja obiteljskih veza svjedoče da vjera može djelovati protiv naslijeđenog nasilja i otuđenja. Kršćanska nada nije poricanje počinjene štete, nego poziv na odgovornost, oproštenje i popravljanje odnosa gdje je to moguće.

Zajednica, molitva i svjedočanstvo drugih pojavljuju se kao sredstva pratnje osobe koja ne može sama izaći iz krize. To odgovara shvaćanju obraćenja kao osobnog, ali ne individualističkog događaja: Bog djeluje i kroz druge, a obnovljena osoba može zatim služiti drugima.

Priča o susretu s osobom na ulici, prihvatu u zajednicu i kasnijem svjedočenju zatvorenicima može promicati kulturu susreta umjesto odbacivanja. Crkveni izvori naglašavaju da ovisnost, bolest i društvena izolacija ne oduzimaju čovjeku dostojanstvo te da su rehabilitacija, potpora i solidarnost stvarna odgovornost zajednice.

Obiteljski život, brak i vjerski odgoj djece prikazani su kao plodovi novog početka, a ne tek kao privatni uspjeh pojedinca. Katoličko razumijevanje obitelji povezuje osobnu vjeru s vjernošću, uzajamnim dostojanstvom i brigom za zajedničko dobro.
concerns: Naslovni kontrast „život bez Boga” i „život s Bogom” može, ako se predstavi previše pojednostavljeno, ostaviti dojam da su ovisnost, nasilje ili psihička bolest samo posljedica manjka vjere. Kršćanska perspektiva može ispoviedati Božje djelovanje u obraćenju, a istodobno priznati složene psihološke, medicinske, obiteljske i društvene čimbenike te potrebu za stručnom pomoći; dostupna struktura ne pokazuje koliko podcast tu razliku razrađuje.

Epizode nasilja prema šefu i ocu te dugogodišnjeg života na ulici traže jasnu moralnu procjenu. Priča o pomirenju ne bi smjela sugerirati da oproštenje ukida odgovornost, pravdu, sigurnost žrtava ili potrebu za popravljanjem štete; obraćenje obuhvaća konkretno odricanje od grijeha i promjenu ponašanja.

Prizori molitve, krunice i dogovora s Isusom na Križevcu mogu biti snažni elementi osobnog svjedočanstva, ali treba paziti da se ne prikažu kao formula koja jamči ozdravljenje ili rješava svaku krizu bez dugotrajnog rada, sakramentalnog i pastoralnog praćenja te ljudske pomoći. Crkveni prikaz obraćenja uključuje trajnu formaciju i životnu promjenu, ne samo presudan trenutak.

Podtema o šizofreniji, epilepsiji, metadonu i psihijatrijskoj ustanovi zahtijeva osobitu osjetljivost: duhovna pratnja ne smije se postaviti kao zamjena za liječenje niti se bolest smije poistovjetiti s moralnom krivnjom. Dostavljeni opis ne omogućuje procjenu kako podcast govori o terapiji, pa je riječ o pastoralnom riziku koji treba uzeti u obzir, a ne o potvrđenom odstupanju.
overall.theological_context: Kršćansko razumijevanje obraćenja u dokumentu Međunarodne teološke komisije povezuje vjeru u Krista s promjenom srca, napuštanjem grijeha, molitvom i konkretnim plodovima u odnosima; ono zato dobro uokviruje prijelaz od ovisnosti i nasilja prema pomirenju i služenju. Apostolska pobudnica Benedikta XVI. Africae munus naglašava trajnost obraćenja, važnost formacije te povezanost svjedočanstva života s jasnim navještajem Krista, što je važno za procjenu misije svjedočenja prikazane u podcastu. Sveto pismo, kako ga sažima isti teološki izvor, ne odvaja oproštenje od promjene života i pomirenja s bližnjim; socijalna dimenzija priče zato uključuje i dostojanstvo bolesnih i ovisnih osoba te zajedničku odgovornost za potporu i rehabilitaciju.

overall.assessment_en: According to the provided structure — and not an independent examination of the complete audio recording — the podcast depicts conversion as a journey from violence, addiction, and despair toward an encounter with Christ, the renewal of relationships, family life, and service to others. Such an emphasis strongly corresponds to the Christian hope that God's call reaches even a person in deep moral and existential crisis, and that conversion manifests itself in a change of life, reconciliation, and solidarity, and not merely in a feeling of faith. The structure also preserves the dignity of a person who was addicted, imprisoned, mentally ill, or homeless, portraying him as a person capable of receiving help, renewing relationships, and contributing to the good of others. The main theological reservations relate to ensuring that mental illnesses and addictions are not reduced to a spiritual problem, that violence is not romanticized as a stage of the past, and that personal testimony is supplemented by clarity regarding responsibility, professional help, and broader social causes of suffering.
overall.theological_context_en: The Christian understanding of conversion in the document of the International Theological Commission links faith in Christ with a change of heart, abandonment of sin, prayer, and concrete fruits in relationships; it therefore frames well the transition from addiction and violence toward reconciliation and service. Benedict XVI's apostolic exhortation Africae munus emphasizes the permanence of conversion, the importance of formation, and the connection between the witness of life and the clear proclamation of Christ, which is important for evaluating the mission of witnessing depicted in the podcast. Sacred Scripture, as summarized by the same theological source, does not separate forgiveness from a change of life and reconciliation with one's neighbor; the social dimension of the story therefore also includes the dignity of sick and addicted persons and the shared responsibility for support and rehabilitation.
seeds_of_logos_en: Conversion is not presented merely as a break with the past, but as a redirection of one's entire life toward God, accompanied by fruits in relationships, family, and service. Christian conversion includes a change of heart, abandonment of sin, and concrete fruits of justice and readiness to forgive.

The motifs of reconciliation with the father and renewal of family ties testify that faith can work against inherited violence and alienation. Christian hope is not a denial of the harm committed, but a call to responsibility, forgiveness, and repairing relationships where possible.

Community, prayer, and the witness of others appear as means of accompanying a person who cannot emerge from crisis alone. This corresponds to the understanding of conversion as a personal, but not individualistic event: God also acts through others, and the renewed person can then serve others.

The story of encountering a person on the street, acceptance into a community, and subsequent witnessing to prisoners can promote a culture of encounter instead of rejection. Church sources emphasize that addiction, illness, and social isolation do not strip a person of dignity, and that rehabilitation, support, and solidarity are a real responsibility of the community.

Family life, marriage, and the religious upbringing of children are presented as the fruits of a new beginning, and not merely as an individual's private success. The Catholic understanding of family links personal faith with fidelity, mutual dignity, and care for the common good.
concerns_en: The titular contrast between “life without God” and “life with God” can, if presented too simplistically, leave the impression that addiction, violence, or mental illness are merely the consequence of a lack of faith. A Christian perspective can profess God's action in conversion while simultaneously acknowledging complex psychological, medical, familial, and social factors and the need for professional help; the available structure does not show to what extent the podcast elaborates this distinction.

The episodes of violence toward the boss and the father and the years of living on the street require a clear moral evaluation. The story of reconciliation should not suggest that forgiveness eliminates responsibility, justice, the safety of victims, or the need to repair harm; conversion encompasses a concrete renunciation of sin and a change of behavior.

The scenes of prayer, the Rosary, and the agreement with Jesus on Križevac can be powerful elements of personal testimony, but care must be taken not to present them as a formula that guarantees healing or resolves every crisis without long-term work, sacramental and pastoral accompaniment, and human help. The Church's presentation of conversion includes ongoing formation and a change of life, not merely a decisive moment.

The subtheme regarding schizophrenia, epilepsy, methadone, and the psychiatric institution requires particular sensitivity: spiritual accompaniment must not be positioned as a replacement for medical treatment, nor may illness be equated with moral guilt. The provided description does not allow an evaluation of how the podcast speaks about therapy, so this is a pastoral risk to be taken into account, rather than a confirmed deviation.

sections.subtitle: Život u dva dijela: bez Boga i s Bogom
sections.screenshot_description: Goran Ćurković pred publikom najavljuje da se njegova životna priča sastoji od dva dijela
sections.content:
Goran Ćurković svjedočanstvo otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, braćo i sestre u Kristu“ i pomalo šaljivim priznanjem: **ljubomoran je na mlade slušatelje** jer su relativno brzo došli do vjere. Sam se, kaže, „morao malo napatiti“, ali dodaje da svatko ima svoj put.

Najavljuje da će ispričati životnu priču koja se sastoji od dva dijela: **prvi bez Boga, drugi s Bogom**. Koji je bolji, ostavlja slušateljima da sami procijene.

Rođen je u Splitu, u katoličkoj obitelji, no u kući nije bilo ni molitve, ni vjere, ni odlaska u crkvu. Roditelji su od njega tražili da ide u crkvu, a on je odbijao jer je gledao njihov primjer: „Ne idete vi, zašto moram ja?“ Otac, kojeg opisuje kao teškog čovjeka, ipak ga je natjerao na vjeronauk.

U crkvi mu je bilo dosadno. Deset Božjih zapovijedi doživljavao je kao popis zabrana: ne smiješ krasti, lagati, psovati ni hodati s tuđim ženama. Zaključio je da je to život „za jednu staru baku koja treba brzo umrijeti“ i da mu ostaje još samo molitva. Bio je uvjeren da u crkvi **nije dobio ništa**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom je usklađen jer opisuje osobno iskustvo i nezrelost tadašnjeg razumijevanja vjere, a ne izričito naučava da su zapovijedi besmislene. Ipak, prikaz zapovijedi gotovo isključivo kao zabrana i zaključak da u crkvi „nije dobio ništa” ostaju nepotpuni ako bi ih se shvatilo kao točan prikaz katoličkog nauka ili svrhe vjeronauka.
concerns: Zapovijedi se prikazuju kao popis ograničenja, bez spominjanja njihova pozitivnog usmjerenja prema ljubavi prema Bogu i bližnjemu.
Rečenica da u crkvi nije dobio ništa može zvučati kao opća tvrdnja o crkvenom životu, iako je u odlomku predstavljena kao njegovo tadašnje osobno iskustvo.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijski prikaz zapovijedi počinje podsjećanjem da je Bog oslobodio svoj narod iz ropstva, pa se Božji zakon prikazuje u kontekstu odnosa i oslobođenja, a ne samo zabrana. Katekizam Ukrajinske Grkokatoličke Crkve opisuje Mojsijev zakon kao odgojitelja koji vodi Kristu; zato zapovijedi nisu cilj same sebi, nego put vjernosti Bogu i dobra za čovjeka.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned because it describes personal experience and the immaturity of the understanding of faith at the time, rather than explicitly teaching that the commandments are meaningless. Nevertheless, the presentation of the commandments almost exclusively as prohibitions and the conclusion that in church he “received nothing” remain incomplete if they were to be understood as an accurate presentation of Catholic teaching or the purpose of catechesis.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The biblical account of the commandments begins by recalling that God delivered his people from slavery, so God's law is presented in the context of relationship and liberation, and not merely prohibitions. The Catechism of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church describes the Law of Moses as a pedagogue leading to Christ; therefore, the commandments are not an end in themselves, but a path of fidelity to God and of good for man.
concerns_en: The commandments are presented as a list of restrictions, without mentioning their positive orientation toward love of God and neighbor.
The sentence that in church he received nothing can sound like a general assertion about church life, even though in the passage it is presented as his personal experience at the time.

sections.subtitle_en: Life in Two Parts: Without God and With God
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran Ćurković announces before the audience that his life story consists of two parts
sections.content_en:
Goran Ćurković opens his testimony with the greeting "Praised be Jesus and Mary, brothers and sisters in Christ" and a somewhat humorous admission: **he is jealous of the young listeners** because they arrived at faith relatively quickly. He himself, he says, "had to suffer a bit," but adds that everyone has their own path.

He announces that he will tell a life story that consists of two parts: **the first without God, the second with God**. Which one is better, he leaves to the listeners to judge for themselves.

He was born in Split, into a Catholic family, but in the house there was neither prayer, nor faith, nor going to church. His parents demanded that he go to church, and he refused because he watched their example: "You don't go, why do I have to?" His father, whom he describes as a difficult man, nevertheless forced him to attend catechism.

He was bored in church. He experienced the Ten Commandments as a list of prohibitions: you must not steal, lie, curse, or run around with other men's wives. He concluded that this was a life "for an old grandma who needs to die soon" and that the only thing left for him was prayer. He was convinced that in church **he received nothing**.

sections.subtitle: Dom obilježen tragedijom i dječak koji je htio biti „frajer“
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje svoje filmske idole iz američkih akcijskih filmova
sections.content:
Obitelj Ćurković pogodilo je nekoliko teških tragedija. Goranova sestra s četiri je godine **pala s petog kata i poginula**, pred majčinim nogama. Brat je s godinu dana obolio od meningitisa i ostao gluhonijem. Majka je stalno plakala i bila depresivna, a budući da u kući nije bilo Boga, počela je piti. Goran o njoj govori sa sućuti: „Jadnica, mislila da s alkoholom će riješiti boli koje je nosila u srcu.“ Otac je bio pomorac, više na brodu nego kod kuće.

Goran je odrastao na ulici ili pred televizorom. Obožavao je američke akcijske filmove, a njihovi glumci postali su mu idoli. Bili su lijepi i tetovirani, imali su velike mišiće, tukli su se i sjedili po zatvorima, a uz to su imali lijepe žene, dobre automobile i puno novca, pušili su Marlboro i pili viski. Iz toga je složio jednostavnu sliku: **muškarac treba biti frajer**.

S deset godina počeo je pušiti i piti alkohol. S jedanaest je bio siguran da zna sve o životu. Dosadili su mu škola, obitelj i svi koji su mu govorili kako se treba ponašati. Zaključio je da je dovoljno velik da živi sam, pa je pobjegao od kuće u drugi grad. Ondje je opljačkao dućan, a policija ga je uhvatila i zatvorila.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje alkohol, krađu i nasilnu sliku muškosti kao dio štetnog životnog obrasca, a majčinu ovisnost opisuje suosjećajno, ne kao razlog za osudu. Važno je zadržati nijansu da tvrdnja kako je počela piti zato što u kući nije bilo Boga predstavlja osobno tumačenje obiteljske priče, a ne opće pravilo o uzroku ovisnosti ili tragedije.
concerns: Povezivanje majčina pijenja s manjkom vjere u kući može pojednostaviti složene psihološke i društvene uzroke ovisnosti, premda je prikazano kao njezina bolna životna okolnost, a ne kao osuda.
Odlomak ne iznosi teološko objašnjenje sestrine smrti; stoga ne bi trebalo zaključivati da je tragedija bila Božja kazna ili posljedica obitelji bez vjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijska mudrost upozorava da opojno piće može zavesti čovjeka jačajući razboritost oslabiti, što se dobro uklapa u prikaz alkohola kao dijela destruktivnog okruženja. Istodobno, katoličko moralno prosuđivanje razlikuje objektivnu pogrešnost čina od osobne krivnje: strah, navika i psihološki ili društveni čimbenici mogu umanjiti odgovornost, pa je suosjećajan prikaz majčine patnje prikladan.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is predominantly aligned with Catholic teaching: it presents alcohol, theft, and a violent image of masculinity as part of a harmful pattern of life, and describes the mother's addiction compassionately, not as a reason for condemnation. It is important to maintain the nuance that the claim that she began drinking because there was no God in the house represents a personal interpretation of the family story, and not a general rule about the cause of addiction or tragedy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical wisdom warns that intoxicating drink can lead man astray and, by strengthening recklessness, weaken discernment, which fits well with the portrayal of alcohol as part of a destructive environment. At the same time, Catholic moral judgment distinguishes the objective wrongness of an act from personal guilt: fear, habit, and psychological or social factors can diminish responsibility, so a compassionate portrayal of the mother's suffering is appropriate.
concerns_en: Linking the mother's drinking to a lack of faith in the house can oversimplify the complex psychological and social causes of addiction, although it is presented as her painful life circumstance, rather than as a condemnation.
The passage does not offer a theological explanation for the sister's death; therefore, one should not conclude that the tragedy was God's punishment or the consequence of a family without faith.

sections.subtitle_en: A Home Marked by Tragedy and a Boy Who Wanted to Be a "Tough Guy"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes his movie idols from American action films
sections.content_en:
The Ćurković family was struck by several severe tragedies. Goran's sister, at four years old, **fell from the fifth floor and died**, at their mother's feet. His brother contracted meningitis at one year old and remained deaf-mute. His mother cried constantly and was depressed, and since there was no God in the house, she began to drink. Goran speaks of her with compassion: "Poor thing, she thought that with alcohol she would resolve the pains she carried in her heart." His father was a sailor, more on the ship than at home.

Goran grew up on the street or in front of the television. He adored American action films, and their actors became his idols. They were handsome and tattooed, had big muscles, fought and sat in prisons, and in addition they had beautiful women, nice cars, and lots of money, smoked Marlboro, and drank whiskey. From that he put together a simple picture: **a man needs to be a tough guy**.

At ten years old he began smoking and drinking alcohol. At eleven he was sure he knew everything about life. He grew tired of school, family, and everyone who told him how he should behave. He concluded that he was big enough to live on his own, so he ran away from home to another city. There he robbed a shop, and the police caught him and locked him up.

sections.subtitle: Otac koji nije znao razgovarati, samo tući
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o odnosu s ocem u kojem nikad nije bilo razgovora
sections.content:
Policija je odmah pozvala oca da dođe po sina, no otac ga je **ostavio tri dana** u pritvoru. Goran objašnjava da je otac razmišljao logično: ako sin ostane koji dan duže, uplašit će se i promijeniti.

Za odnos s ocem kaže da ne zna može li ga se uopće tako nazvati. Ističe da mu je otac dobar čovjek, ali s jednim velikim problemom: **nije znao komunicirati**. U kući nikad nije bilo razgovora, a cijeli odgoj svodio se na batine. Otac je vjerovao da će batinama riješiti sve probleme.

Kad je nakon tri dana došao po njega, ništa ga nije pitao. Odmah ga je pretukao u policijskoj stanici, i to toliko da je **policija morala braniti dječaka od vlastitog oca**. Tukao ga je zatim još dva i pol sata u autobusu na putu kući.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak prikazuje očevu batinu kao nasilje koje je dječaku nanijelo štetu, a ne kao opravdano kršćansko odgojno sredstvo, pa sam po sebi nije u sukobu s katoličkim naukom. Ipak, ne izriče izravno razliku između odgojne discipline i zlostavljanja.
concerns: Bez dodatnog konteksta netko bi biblijske retke o tjelesnom kažnjavanju mogao pogrešno shvatiti kao opravdanje za premlaćivanje; odlomak bi jasnije osudio takvo nasilje.
magisterium.enrichment: Sirah govori o disciplini, ali ovaj opis dugotrajnog i teškog premlaćivanja valja promatrati u svjetlu štete koju fizičko zlostavljanje može nanijeti djetetu i kasnijim odnosima. Katolički dokument o zaštiti života izričito prepoznaje fizičko zlostavljanje djece kao oblik zlostavljanja te ističe njegove dugotrajne posljedice, kao i važnost liječenja i zaštite djece.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage portrays the father's beating as violence that caused harm to the boy, rather than as a justified Christian disciplinary measure, so in itself it is not in conflict with Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, it does not directly state the distinction between educational discipline and abuse.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Sirach speaks of discipline, but this description of prolonged and severe beating must be viewed in light of the harm that physical abuse can inflict on a child and subsequent relationships. A Catholic document on the protection of life explicitly recognizes the physical abuse of children as a form of abuse and highlights its long-term consequences, as well as the importance of treatment and child protection.
concerns_en: Without additional context, someone could misunderstand the biblical verses on corporal punishment as a justification for beatings; the passage would condemn such violence more clearly.

sections.subtitle_en: A Father Who Did Not Know How to Talk, Only How to Beat
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran speaks about the relationship with his father in which there was never any conversation
sections.content_en:
The police immediately called his father to come get his son, but his father **left him for three days** in custody. Goran explains that his father thought logically: if the son stays a few days longer, he will get scared and change.

About the relationship with his father, he says he does not know whether it can be called that at all. He emphasizes that his father is a good man, but with one big problem: **he did not know how to communicate**. In the house there was never any conversation, and his entire upbringing came down to beatings. His father believed that he would solve all problems with beatings.

When he came to get him after three days, he asked him nothing. He beat him immediately in the police station, and that so severely that **the police had to defend the boy from his own father**. He then beat him for another two and a half hours on the bus on the way home.

sections.subtitle: Majčina smrt, mržnja i metak na prvu godišnjicu
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava datum 2. lipnja 1978. i pokušaj samoubojstva pištoljem
sections.content:
Kad je Goranu bilo trinaest godina, umrla mu je majka. Zapao je u depresiju jer je nikad nije zagrlio ni poljubio i nikad joj nije rekao da je voli. A volio ju je i bezbroj puta poželio pokazati tu ljubav. Nije mogao jer je vjerovao da **muškarac ne smije pokazivati osjećaje** i da su osjećaji za žene. Ta ga je bol dovela do odluke da se ubije.

Osam mjeseci nakon majčine smrti otac se ponovno oženio. Tada se u Goranu **prvi put javila mržnja** prema ocu jer nije mogao shvatiti kako je nakon osam mjeseci „zaboravio“ njegovu majku. Mrzio je i brata, kojemu je, kako je tada mislio, sve bilo svejedno i koji je i sam postao alkoholičar. Mrzio je i ženu koja je, po njegovim riječima, došla „glumiti majku“.

Na **2. lipnja 1978.**, prvu godišnjicu majčine smrti, posudio je pištolj od prijatelja. Otac je kod kuće gledao Svjetsko nogometno prvenstvo u Argentini. Goran je sjeo blizu njega jer je htio razgovarati, no otac se nervozno okrenuo, udario ga i potjerao u sobu. U sobi je uzeo pištolj i pucao sebi u glavu.

Probudio se u bolnici i čuo liječnika kako govori da operacija nije uspjela: **metak je ostao u glavi**, ne može se izvaditi, Goran neće dugo živjeti i imat će velikih problema s glavom. Nekoliko dana kasnije otac i maćeha rekli su mu da je sve u redu i da je metak izvađen. Njemu je bilo svejedno. Zapao je u još dublju depresiju jer se nije uspio ubiti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje pokušaj samoubojstva kao posljedicu duboke boli i očaja, ali ga ne prikazuje kao dobar ili poželjan čin, pa nema izričitog proturječja katoličkom nauku. Ipak, budući da ozbiljno samouništenje ostaje bez izravne teološke procjene, čitatelju može ostati nejasno kako Crkva vrednuje taj čin.
concerns: Odlomak ne navodi da je samoubojstvo teško protivno ljubavi prema sebi, bližnjemu i Bogu; pritom se iz samog svjedočanstva ne može procijeniti osobna odgovornost osobe u tom trenutku.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk smatra samoubojstvo ozbiljno protivnim ljubavi prema sebi, jer je ljudski život dar koji čovjek ne posjeduje kao apsolutni gospodar; ono također ranjava odnose solidarnosti s bližnjima i protivi se ljubavi prema Bogu. Biblijska i kršćanska vjera ipak ne zahtijevaju poricanje žalosti: sveti Jeronim otvoreno govori o suzama i boli nakon gubitka, što pomaže razlikovati žalovanje od odobravanja samouništenja.

citations.document_author: Eusebius Sophronius Hieronymus (Jerome of Stridon or St. Jerome)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes a suicide attempt as a consequence of deep pain and despair, but does not present it as a good or desirable act, so there is no explicit contradiction of Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, since serious self-destruction remains without direct theological evaluation, it may remain unclear to the reader how the Church evaluates this act.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching considers suicide to be gravely contrary to love of self, because human life is a gift that man does not possess as absolute master; it also wounds relationships of solidarity with neighbors and contradicts love of God. Biblical and Christian faith nevertheless do not demand the denial of sorrow: Saint Jerome speaks openly of tears and pain after a loss, which helps distinguish mourning from the approval of self-destruction.
concerns_en: The passage does not state that suicide is gravely contrary to love of self, neighbor, and God; moreover, from the testimony itself one cannot assess the personal responsibility of the person at that moment.

sections.subtitle_en: Mother's Death, Hatred, and a Bullet on the First Anniversary
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts the date of June 2, 1978, and the suicide attempt with a gun
sections.content_en:
When Goran was thirteen years old, his mother died. He fell into depression because he had never hugged or kissed her and had never told her that he loved her. And he loved her and countless times wished to show that love. He could not because he believed that **a man must not show feelings** and that feelings are for women. That pain brought him to the decision to kill himself.

Eight months after his mother's death, his father remarried. At that point, in Goran **for the first time hatred arose** toward his father because he could not understand how after eight months he had "forgotten" his mother. He also hated his brother, to whom, as he thought then, nothing mattered and who also became an alcoholic himself. He also hated the woman who, in his words, came to "act like a mother."

On **June 2, 1978**, the first anniversary of his mother's death, he borrowed a gun from a friend. His father was at home watching the World Cup in Argentina. Goran sat down near him because he wanted to talk, but his father turned around nervously, hit him, and chased him into his room. In the room, he took the gun and shot himself in the head.

He woke up in the hospital and heard the doctor saying that the surgery had not succeeded: **the bullet remained in his head**, it could not be removed, Goran would not live long and would have major problems with his head. A few days later, his father and stepmother told him that everything was fine and that the bullet had been removed. To him it was all the same. He fell into an even deeper depression because he had not succeeded in killing himself.

sections.subtitle: „Bezopasna“ trava, epilepsija i heroin
sections.screenshot_description: Goran ironično prepričava kako su ga prijatelji nagovarali na marihuanu
sections.content:
Nakon izlaska iz bolnice Goran je uz alkohol počeo uzimati i tablete. Uvijek se družio sa starijima, a oni su već dugo pušili marihuanu i hašiš. Svaki dan su ga uvjeravali da je marihuana prirodna biljka koja je dobra za zdravlje: razvija mozak, popravlja san i apetit, ne izaziva agresiju ni krizu i ne stvara ovisnost.

Na kraju je probao. Idućih deset dana nije pušio i ponosno je zaključio da je „čovjek od karaktera“ i da svi lažu kad govore o opasnosti. Nakon deset dana zapalio je ponovno, a uskoro je **pušio od jutra do mraka, svaki dan**.

Jednog se dana probudio u bolnici, razbijene i krvave glave. Liječnici su postavili dijagnozu: **epilepsija grand mal**. Bolesti se stidio i zapao je u još težu depresiju. Znao je da mora promijeniti život, ali nije znao kako: otac je bio na brodu, brat svaki dan pijan, a maćeha ga se bojala jer je prema njoj bio agresivan i za sve krivio nju.

S gorkom ironijom zahvaljuje Bogu na „prijateljima“ koji su ga nagovorili na **heroin**, uz obećanje da će njime riješiti sve probleme. Bio je uvjeren da gore ne može biti. Prvi doživljaj euforije opisuje kao „super“. U početku je trebao malo novca za malo heroina, ali potrebe su brzo rasle. Počeo je **krasti automobile, provaljivati u kuće, stanove i restorane te krasti novčanike**, radio je stvari za koje je bio siguran da ih nikad neće raditi.

Ističe i paradoks: otac je cijeli život zarađivao i donosio stvari u kuću, a Goran je **za samo mjesec dana sve pokrao i prodao**. Oca je uhvatila panika.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom jer prikazuje opasnosti ovisnosti i njezine štetne posljedice, a uporabu droga ne predstavlja kao poželjnu niti je opravdava. Tvrdnje o navodnoj korisnosti marihuane izričito su pripisane Goranovim poznanicima, pa se ne mogu čitati kao potvrda pripovjedača.
concerns: Zablude o marihuani prenesene su, ali nisu izravno ispravljene; stoga bi slušatelj mogao poželjeti jasnije upozorenje da se ne radi o bezopasnoj biljci i da o liječenju treba odlučivati uz stručni medicinski savjet.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje upozorava na štetu droga za zdravlje, razum, slobodu i društvene odnose, ali razlikuje rekreativno drogiranje od strogo nadzirane uporabe psihotropnih lijekova u opravdane medicinske svrhe. Ovisnost može ozbiljno narušiti slobodu i osobnu odgovornost, pa je primjereno spojiti istinu o štetnosti droga sa suosjećanjem prema osobi koja se bori s ovisnošću.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Catholic perspective because it portrays the dangers of addiction and its harmful consequences, and does not present drug use as desirable or justify it. Claims about the alleged usefulness of marijuana are explicitly attributed to Goran's acquaintances, so they cannot be read as an endorsement by the narrator.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching warns against the harm of drugs to health, reason, freedom, and social relationships, but distinguishes recreational drug use from the strictly controlled use of psychotropic medications for justified medical purposes. Addiction can severely impair freedom and personal responsibility, so it is appropriate to combine the truth about the harmfulness of drugs with compassion for the person struggling with addiction.
concerns_en: Misconceptions about marijuana are recounted, but not directly corrected; therefore, a listener might desire a clearer warning that it is not a harmless plant and that medical decisions regarding treatment should be made with professional medical advice.

sections.subtitle_en: "Harmless" Weed, Epilepsy, and Heroin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran ironically recounts how his friends persuaded him into marijuana
sections.content_en:
After leaving the hospital, along with alcohol Goran also began taking pills. He always hung out with older people, and they had already been smoking marijuana and hashish for a long time. Every day they persuaded him that marijuana is a natural plant that is good for health: it develops the brain, improves sleep and appetite, does not cause aggression or withdrawal, and does not create addiction.

In the end he tried it. For the next ten days he did not smoke and proudly concluded that he was a "man of character" and that everyone was lying when talking about danger. After ten days he lit up again, and soon **he was smoking from morning till night, every day**.

One day he woke up in the hospital, his head smashed and bloody. The doctors made a diagnosis: **grand mal epilepsy**. He was ashamed of the illness and fell into an even more severe depression. He knew he had to change his life, but he did not know how: his father was on the ship, his brother drunk every day, and his stepmother was afraid of him because he was aggressive toward her and blamed her for everything.

With bitter irony he thanks God for the "friends" who talked him into **heroin**, with the promise that with it he would solve all problems. He was convinced that it could not get worse. He describes the first experience of euphoria as "super." In the beginning he needed a little money for a little heroin, but the needs grew quickly. He began **stealing cars, breaking into houses, apartments, and restaurants, and stealing wallets**, doing things he was certain he would never do.

He also points out a paradox: his father had worked and brought things into the house his whole life, and Goran **in just one month stole and sold everything**. Panic seized his father.

sections.subtitle: „Čekam te već 20 godina“: zatvor i psihijatrija kao godišnji odmor
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava očev zakašnjeli poziv na razgovor
sections.content:
Jednog je dana otac u suzama pozvao Gorana: „Gorane, sine, imaš velikih problema. Ajde, sjedi, idemo razgovarati, ja ti hoću pomoći.“ Goran mu je odgovorio da ga čeka **već dvadeset godina** i da je sada kasno.

Bile su to osamdesete, vrijeme komunizma, kada nije bilo centara, savjetovališta ni zajednica. Otac nije znao gdje potražiti pomoć pa je otišao na policiju. Jednog su jutra policajci ušli u Goranovu sobu, bacili mu heroin pokraj glave i proglasili ga dilerom. Goran objašnjava da su mu htjeli pomoći: ako ga zatvore pet-šest mjeseci, možda će shvatiti da je na krivom putu.

Dogodilo se suprotno. U zatvoru je naučio **kako bolje krasti i kako miješati drogu da je ima više**. Droge, alkohola i tableta bilo je jednako kao vani. Izašao je „pametniji nego što je ušao“, a zatvor mu je, kaže, napravio sto puta gore.

Otac je nastavio tražiti pomoć. Jedan njegov prijatelj rekao mu je: „Marko, tvoj sin Goran je bolestan“ i savjetovao da ga se smjesti na psihijatriju jer mu „nitko ne može pomoći nego doktori“. Obitelj je bila sretna. Goran nije htio ići, ali zbog problema sa sudom i policijom morao je. Dva dana prije prijema sve je organizirao.

Psihijatrija u Splitu bila je u prizemlju. Imao je svoj krevet, cijeli dan gledao televiziju i šalio se s pacijentima, liječnici su mu davali tablete, a prijatelji su mu svaki dan **kroz prozor dobacivali drogu i alkohol**. Bilo mu je „kao na godišnjem odmoru“. Jedne je večeri u pidžami s natpisom psihijatrije pobjegao u diskoteku, gdje je plesao i opijao se, dok ga policija nije pretukla i vratila. Liječnici nisu znali što bi s njim jer je remetio sve, pa su ga na kraju izbacili. Kod kuće je nastao pakao: svaki dan policija, hitna pomoć, tučnjave i pijani brat.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje zatvor i psihijatrijsku ustanovu kroz osobno svjedočanstvo te ne iznosi izravnu tvrdnju da su takvi postupci općenito katolički prihvatljivi ili djelotvorni. Ipak, formulacija da je policijska podvala bila zamišljena kao pomoć ostaje morałno nejasna, jer dobra namjera ei opravdala bi laganje ili nepravedno postupanje.
concerns: Priča bi mogla ostaviti dojam da su prijevara, zatvaranje ili neprimjereno psihijatrijsko zbrinjavanje prihvatljivi načini liječenja ovisnosti; katolička procjena treba razlikovati nečiju namjeru pomoći od moralne ispravnosti i stvarnih posljedica postupka.
Pojedinačno iskustvo u psihijatrijskoj ustanovi ne treba generalizirati kao prosudbu psihijatrijskog liječenja ili liječnika općenito.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pristup ovisnosti povezuje osobnu odgovornost s priznanjem ranjivosti i potrebom za stručnom pomoći; skrb treba poštovati dostojanstvo osobe te odgovarati njezinim stvarnim potrebama. Crkva također potiče obiteljsku potporu, prevenciju i pristup ustanovama koje mogu pružiti skrb, a ne očaj ili napuštanje osobe koja pati.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes prison and the psychiatric institution through personal testimony and does not make a direct claim that such practices are generally Catholically acceptable or effective. Nevertheless, the formulation that the police setup was intended as help remains morally unclear, because a good intention would not justify lying or unjust treatment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic approach to addiction links personal responsibility with the acknowledgment of vulnerability and the need for professional help; care must respect the dignity of the person and respond to their real needs. The Church also encourages family support, prevention, and access to institutions that can provide care, rather than despair or the abandonment of the person who suffers.
concerns_en: The story could leave the impression that deceit, confinement, or inadequate psychiatric placement are acceptable ways to treat addiction; a Catholic evaluation must distinguish someone's intention to help from the moral correctness and actual consequences of the action.
An individual experience in a psychiatric institution should not be generalized as a judgment on psychiatric treatment or physicians in general.

sections.subtitle_en: "I Have Been Waiting for You for 20 Years": Prison and Psychiatry as a Vacation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts his father's belated invitation to talk
sections.content_en:
One day his father called Goran in tears: "Goran, son, you have big problems. Come on, sit down, let's talk, I want to help you." Goran answered him that he had been waiting for him **for twenty years already** and that now it was too late.

Those were the eighties, the time of communism, when there were no centers, counseling services, or communities. His father did not know where to seek help, so he went to the police. One morning police officers entered Goran's room, threw heroin beside his head, and proclaimed him a dealer. Goran explains that they wanted to help him: if they locked him up for five or six months, maybe he would realize that he was on the wrong path.

The opposite happened. In prison he learned **how to steal better and how to mix drugs so there would be more**. There were just as many drugs, alcohol, and pills as outside. He came out "smarter than he went in," and prison, he says, made him a hundred times worse.

His father continued to seek help. A friend of his told him: "Marko, your son Goran is sick" and advised that he be placed in psychiatry because "no one can help him but doctors." The family was happy. Goran did not want to go, but because of problems with the court and the police he had to. Two days before admission, he organized everything.

Psychiatry in Split was on the ground floor. He had his bed, watched television all day and joked with patients, the doctors gave him pills, and his friends **threw drugs and alcohol to him through the window** every day. To him it was "like on vacation." One evening, in pajamas with the psychiatry's inscription, he escaped to a disco, where he danced and got drunk until the police beat him and brought him back. The doctors did not know what to do with him because he disrupted everything, so in the end they kicked him out. At home hell broke loose: every day police, emergency medical service, fights, and a drunk brother.

sections.subtitle: Posao u skladištu, nož na šefa i nož u očev trbuh
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje sukob s ocem koji je završio ubodom nožem
sections.content:
Otac je, kao roditelj, htio pružiti sinu još jednu priliku. Drugi mu je prijatelj savjetovao: „Marko, Goranu trebaš naći posao.“ Računica je opet bila logična: Goran će ustajati rano, raditi osam sati, umoriti se i neće imati ni volje ni vremena za gluposti.

Goran nije htio raditi jer mu je bilo lakše krasti. Tada se okupila cijela rodbina i dala mu ultimátum: **„Radi ili na ulicu.“** Od dva zla izabrao je manje i pristao raditi.

Otac mu je našao posao u skladištu firme u kojoj je i sam radio, sa svime potrebnim za mornare i brodove. Ondje su radili očevi prijatelji, koji su obećali da će se pobrinuti za njega, ako treba ga i istući, i dati mu toliko posla „da će mu se pariti iz ušiju“. Goran to naziva **najvećom očevom pogreškom**. Pokrao je pola skladišta, prodao sve što se moglo prodati i posuđivao novac koji nikome nije vraćao. Jednog se dana naljutio na šefa i **jurio ga nožem po skladištu**. Odmah je dobio otkaz.

Zatim je došao kraj. Pijan i u krizi, tražio je od oca novac. Otac ga je udario šakom u glavu i počeli su se tući. Otac je imao 120 kilograma, a Goran je, vidjevši da će dobiti batine, **uzeo nož i ubo oca u trbuh**. Otac je završio u bolnici, Goran u zatvoru.

I dalje je bio ljut na oca: da mu je dao novac, kupio bi drogu i ništa se ne bi dogodilo. Nakon zatvora htio se vratiti kući kao da se ništa nije dogodilo. Danas kaže da je **potpuni nedostatak savjesti** nešto najgore što se čovjeku može dogoditi. Vrata su bila zaključana, a otac mu je kroz njih rekao: „Između obitelji i ulice, ti si izabrao ulicu. Živi na ulici. Ako odlučiš mijenjati život, dođi, mi ćemo ti pomoći.“ Mržnja je u tom trenutku narasla „milijun puta“. Pljunuo je na vrata, proklinjao i otišao uz riječi da ga otac više nikad neće vidjeti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer krađu i nasilje ne prikazuje kao opravdane, a „potpuni nedostatak savjesti” prepoznaje kao ozbiljno zlo. Ipak, sažetak ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se prosudila osobna krivnja s obzirom na ovisnost i okolnosti, niti očev udarac treba shvatiti kao opravdan odgovor na sinovljevo ponašanje.
concerns: Očev fizički udarac i Goranov ubod nožem prikazani su kao dio eskalacije sukoba; bilo bi važno ne protumačiti očev udarac kao moralno opravdan niti ga koristiti za umanjivanje odgovornosti za nasilje.
Očevo postavljanje granice može se razumjeti u kontekstu sigurnosti i odgovornosti, ali sažetak ne razjašnjava kako su se u obitelji istodobno čuvali dostojanstvo, pomoć i mogućnost pomirenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pogled drži čovjeka moralno odgovornim, ali priznanje grijeha nije poziv na očaj: ono otvara put obraćenju i povjerenju u Božje milosrđe. Biblijska slika izgubljenoga sina i Isusova potraga za izgubljenima pokazuju da su pokajanje, promjena života i pomirenje mogući, dok pravda uključuje odgovornost i nastoji voditi obnovi, a ne samo kazni.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching because it does not portray theft and violence as justified, and recognizes a “complete lack of conscience” as a serious evil. Nevertheless, the summary does not provide enough data to judge personal culpability with regard to addiction and circumstances, nor should the father's strike be understood as a justified response to the son's behavior.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic view holds man morally responsible, but the acknowledgment of sin is not a call to despair: it opens the way to conversion and trust in God's mercy. The biblical image of the prodigal son and Jesus' search for the lost show that repentance, a change of life, and reconciliation are possible, while justice includes responsibility and seeks to lead to renewal, rather than merely punishment.
concerns_en: The father's physical blow and Goran's stabbing with a knife are presented as part of an escalation of conflict; it would be important not to interpret the father's strike as morally justified nor to use it to diminish responsibility for violence.

The father's setting of boundaries can be understood in the context of safety and responsibility, but the summary does not clarify how dignity, help, and the possibility of reconciliation were simultaneously preserved in the family.

sections.subtitle_en: A Job in the Warehouse, a Knife at the Boss, and a Knife in His Father's Stomach
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes the conflict with his father that ended with a knife stabbing
sections.content_en:
His father, as a parent, wanted to give his son another chance. Another friend advised him: "Marko, you need to find Goran a job." The logic was again sound: Goran would get up early, work eight hours, get tired, and have neither the will nor the time for foolishness.

Goran did not want to work because it was easier for him to steal. Then the whole extended family gathered and gave him an ultimatum: **"Work or out on the street."** Of two evils he chose the lesser and agreed to work.

His father found him a job in the warehouse of the company where he worked himself, with everything needed for sailors and ships. His father's friends worked there, and they promised that they would take care of him, beat him if necessary, and give him so much work "that steam would come out of his ears." Goran calls this **his father's biggest mistake**. He stole half the warehouse, sold everything that could be sold, and borrowed money that he returned to no one. One day he got angry at his boss and **chased him with a knife around the warehouse**. He was fired immediately.

Then came the end. Drunk and in withdrawal, he asked his father for money. His father hit him with a fist in the head, and they started fighting. His father weighed 120 kilograms, and Goran, seeing that he would get a beating, **took a knife and stabbed his father in the stomach**. His father ended up in the hospital, Goran in prison.

He was still angry with his father: if he had given him the money, he would have bought drugs and nothing would have happened. After prison he wanted to return home as if nothing had happened. Today he says that a **complete lack of conscience** is the worst thing that can happen to a man. The door was locked, and his father told him through it: "Between family and the street, you chose the street. Live on the street. If you decide to change your life, come, we will help you." Hatred at that moment grew "a million times." He spat on the door, cursed, and left with the words that his father would never see him again.

sections.subtitle: Devet godina na ulici, šizofrenija i Popovača u ratu
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o dijagnozi šizofrenije i odlasku u Popovaču
sections.content:
Goran je **devet godina živio na ulici kao klošar** i to razdoblje naziva katastrofom. Dok je imao novca i droge, imao je i prijatelja jer je vani sve interes. Došao je do točke kada čak ni tada nitko nije htio biti s njim, toliko je ružno izgledao i nenormalno se ponašao.

Pred kraj života na ulici javili su se **abnormalni strahovi** koje ne može opisati, strahovi „za poluditi, od svega“. Nijedna droga ni tableta nisu ga mogle smiriti. Smirivala ga je samo vlastita krv: rezao se, praznom injekcijom vadio krv, pio je i mazao po sebi.

Kad su ga posljednji put zatvorili, neuropsihijatar u zatvoru postavio je dijagnozu **šizofrenije**. Iz Remetinca je čekao prijevoz na psihijatriju, a tada je počeo rat u Hrvatskoj. Budući da su se prvi kreveti oslobodili na **trećem patološkom odjelu u Popovači**, Goran je s dvojicom mladića završio na odjelu na kojem su bili ubojice. Terapija ga je smirila, ali jednog je jutra za stolom shvatio: „Što ja ovdje radim? Ja sam obični narkoman.“ Bio je uvjeren da će ga ubiti za dva dana, pa je čekao priliku, **ukrao novac kolegi pacijentu i pobjegao**.

U glavi je složio „genijalan“ plan: vratiti se u Split, malo se drogirati, otići u rat, Hrvatska će pobijediti, vlast će se promijeniti i on će biti slobodan. Jednog je jutra ušao u vojarnu i izjavio da kao Hrvat ide braniti državu. Vojnik mu je odgovorio da se okrene i izađe jer će mu slomiti obje noge. Goran se danas tome smije: sada ima 90 kilograma, a tada nije imao ni 60, „sama kost i koža“. Priznaje da bi kalašnjikov, da su mu ga dali, sigurno prodao ili zamijenio za heroin.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje tešku patnju, samoozljeđivanje, krađu i bijeg bez vidljivog opravdavanja tih postupaka; kao svjedočanstvo o destruktivnim posljedicama života obilježenog drogom, stoga ne proturječi katoličkom nauku. Sažetak, međutim, ne omogućuje procjenu Goranove osobne moralne odgovornosti ni valjanosti tadašnje dijagnoze, a psihičku bolest ne bi trebalo poistovjetiti s moralnom pokvarenošću.
concerns: Opis osobe kao „nenormalne” prenesen je kao Goranova procjena vlastitog tadašnjeg ponašanja; bez dodatnog konteksta postoji rizik stigmatiziranja osoba s psihičkim bolestima.
Krađa novca od drugog pacijenta i bijeg prikazani su kao dio njegova plana, ali sažetak ne navodi posljedice ni eventualnu naknadu štete.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje grijeha priznaje ljudsku odgovornost, ali i dostojanstvo osobe koja je počinila zlo; kažnjavanje ne bi trebalo biti samo odmazda, nego treba težiti popravljanju štete, rehabilitaciji i ponovnom uključivanju u zajednicu. Sveto pismo prikazuje obraćenje kao put koji može uključivati više padova i novih početaka te upozorava da priznanje grijeha vodi nadi, a ne očaju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes severe suffering, self-harm, theft, and escape without visible justification of these actions; as a testimony to the destructive consequences of a life marked by drugs, it therefore does not contradict Catholic teaching. The summary, however, does not allow an evaluation of Goran's personal moral responsibility nor the validity of the diagnosis at the time, and mental illness should not be equated with moral depravity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of sin acknowledges human responsibility, but also the dignity of the person who has committed evil; punishment should not be mere retribution, but must aim at repairing harm, rehabilitation, and reintegration into the community. Sacred Scripture presents conversion as a journey that can include multiple falls and new beginnings, and warns that the acknowledgment of sin leads to hope, not despair.
concerns_en: The description of the person as “abnormal” is recounted as Goran's assessment of his own behavior at the time; without additional context, there is a risk of stigmatizing persons with mental illnesses.
The theft of money from another patient and the escape are presented as part of his plan, but the summary does not state the consequences or eventual restitution.

sections.subtitle_en: Nine Years on the Street, Schizophrenia, and Popovača During the War
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran talks about the diagnosis of schizophrenia and going to Popovača
sections.content_en:
Goran **lived on the street for nine years as a tramp** and calls that period a catastrophe. While he had money and drugs, he had friends because outside everything is interest. He reached the point where even then no one wanted to be with him, so hideous did he look and so abnormally did he behave.

Toward the end of life on the street, **abnormal fears** arose that he cannot describe, fears "to drive you crazy, of everything." No drug or pill could calm him down. Only his own blood calmed him down: he cut himself, drew blood with an empty syringe, drank it, and smeared it on himself.

When they locked him up for the last time, the neuropsychiatrist in prison made a diagnosis of **schizophrenia**. From Remetinec he waited for transport to psychiatry, and at that time the war in Croatia began. Since the first beds opened up in the **third pathological ward in Popovača**, Goran ended up with two young men in the ward where murderers were kept. The therapy calmed him down, but one morning at the table he realized: "What am I doing here? I am an ordinary junkie." He was convinced that they would kill him in two days, so he waited for an opportunity, **stole money from a fellow patient, and escaped**.

In his head he put together an "ingenious" plan: return to Split, take a few drugs, go to war, Croatia will win, the government will change, and he will be free. One morning he entered a barracks and stated that as a Croat he was going to defend the country. A soldier replied to him to turn around and get out because he would break both of his legs. Goran laughs at that today: now he weighs 90 kilograms, and back then he didn't even weigh 60, "pure skin and bone." He admits that if they had given him a Kalashnikov, he surely would have sold it or traded it for heroin.

sections.subtitle: Pet dana pod pogledom ubojice i neočekivano prijateljstvo
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje pet dana zavezan u sobi s pacijentom kojemu je ukrao novac
sections.content:
Policija je raspisala tjeralicu i Goran je ubrzo uhvaćen te vraćen u Popovaču. Dvojicu tehničara, **Besima i Rifata**, kaže, nikad neće zaboraviti. Pretukli su ga, stavili mu luđačku košulju i zavezali noge za šipke kreveta, „kao zagrebačku salamu“.

Namjerno su ga, kako bi ga kaznili, smjestili u sobu s pacijentom kojemu je ukrao novac, čovjekom koji je **ubio četvero ljudi**. Goran mu je novac uzeo upravo zato što je bio siguran da se nikad neće vratiti. Pet dana taj je čovjek sjedio na krevetu nasuprot njemu, pušio i gledao ga u oči, ne izgovorivši ni riječ. To ga je psihički uništavalo. Svaki put kad bi se čovjek ustao, Goran je mislio da je kraj.

Peti dan čovjek je progovorio: „Ti znaš tko sam ja, što sam napravio i što mogu napraviti.“ Priznao je da je pet dana razmišljao hoće li ga zadaviti, a onda dodao: „Kad si imao hrabrosti meni ukrasti novac, svaka ti čast.“ Goran to naziva „najljepšim trenutkom u životu“. Postali su **najbolji prijatelji**, a za Dragu kaže da je bio dobar.

O Popovači bi, kaže, mogao napisati knjigu. Sve je funkcioniralo dok je bilo lijekova, ali u ratu ih često nije bilo, a zamjene su bile slabe i nastajao je „cirkus“. Ipak, bilo je i lijepih dana.

Pri izlasku pozvao ga je glavni liječnik, **primarijus Milivoj Koludrović**, i upozorio ga: ako počini još jedno kazneno djelo, osobno će ga vratiti i ondje će umrijeti. Goran je odlučio promijeniti život. Vratio se u Split, a prva vrata na koja je pokucao bila su **vrata dilera**. Već sljedećeg popodneva vratio se na staro.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim pogledom jer opisuje osobno iskustvo, recidiv i neočekivano prijateljstvo, a ne tvrdi da je nasilje ili povratak drogama moralno dobar. Ipak, opis smještanja kao kazne u sobu s čovjekom koji mu je prijetio ne treba čitati kao opravdanje takvog postupanja; kršćansko shvaćanje kazne naglašava pravednost, razumnost i rehabilitaciju, a ne osvetu.
concerns: Odlomak ne daje jasnu moralnu prosudbu premlaćivanja i zastrašivanja koje opisuje; ako je smještanje s opasnim pacijentom doista bilo namjerna kazna, valja ga razlikovati od legitimne zaštite i liječenja.
Prvi povratak dileru prikazan je kao porazan recidiv, ali odlomak ne razrađuje odgovornost, liječenje ni potporu koja bi mogla pomoći u promjeni.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje pravedne kazne povezuje zaštitu zajednice s mogućnošću promjene i rehabilitacije počinitelja, a ne s pukim kažnjavanjem. Neočekivano prijateljstvo može se čitati kao znak da odnos i povjerenje mogu nastati i nakon ozbiljnog prijestupa, ali ono ne čini prijetnju ili nasilje prihvatljivima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Catholic perspective because it describes personal experience, relapse, and an unexpected friendship, rather than asserting that violence or returning to drugs is morally good. Nevertheless, the description of being placed as punishment in a room with a man who threatened him should not be read as a justification of such treatment; the Christian understanding of punishment emphasizes justice, reasonableness, and rehabilitation, rather than vengeance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of just punishment links the protection of the community with the possibility of reform and rehabilitation of the offender, rather than mere retribution. An unexpected friendship can be read as a sign that relationship and trust can arise even after a serious transgression, but it does not make threats or violence acceptable.
concerns_en: The passage does not provide a clear moral judgment on the beating and intimidation it describes; if placement with a dangerous patient was indeed an intentional punishment, it must be distinguished from legitimate protection and treatment.
The first return to the dealer is presented as a crushing relapse, but the passage does not elaborate on responsibility, treatment, or the support that could help bring about change.

sections.subtitle_en: Five Days Under a Murderer's Gaze and an Unexpected Friendship
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes five days tied up in a room with the patient from whom he had stolen money
sections.content_en:
The police issued a warrant and Goran was soon caught and returned to Popovača. The two technicians, **Besim and Rifat**, he says, he will never forget. They beat him, put him in a straitjacket, and tied his legs to the bed bars, "like a Zagreb salami."

Deliberately, in order to punish him, they placed him in a room with the patient from whom he had stolen money, a man who had **killed four people**. Goran had taken his money precisely because he was sure he would never return. For five days that man sat on the bed opposite him, smoked, and looked him in the eyes, without uttering a word. That was destroying him mentally. Every time the man stood up, Goran thought it was the end.

On the fifth day the man spoke: "You know who I am, what I did, and what I can do." He admitted that for five days he had been thinking about whether to strangle him, and then added: "Since you had the guts to steal money from me, kudos to you." Goran calls that the "most beautiful moment in life." They became **best friends**, and about Drago he says that he was good.

About Popovača, he says, he could write a book. Everything functioned while there were medications, but during the war they were often unavailable, and the substitutes were weak and a "circus" ensued. Still, there were also beautiful days.

Upon leaving, the chief physician, **Chief Physician Milivoj Koludrović**, called him in and warned him: if he commits one more criminal offense, he will personally bring him back and he will die there. Goran decided to change his life. He returned to Split, and the first door he knocked on was **the dealer's door**. By the very next afternoon he returned to his old ways.

sections.subtitle: Najdublje dno: kad je smrt izgledala kao spas
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o preziru prolaznika i želji za smrću
sections.content:
Goran više nije mogao spavati. Jedan sendvič nosio bi u džepu po dvadeset dana ili mjesec dana i to mu je bila sva hrana. Bio je **pun živih otvorenih rana** i širio je smrad koji, kaže, slušatelji ne mogu ni zamisliti. Kad bi ušao u gradski autobus, svi bi na sljedećoj stanici izašli, pa je uvijek imao gdje sjesti.

Sjedio bi skupljen na zidu, a prolaznici su ga pljuvali, tukli šakama i nogama te vikali da ga treba ubiti jer je **„otrov za djecu“**. Njemu je bilo svejedno. Čekao je samo smrt jer mu je **smrt bila spas, a život samo patnja**. Bezbroj puta popio bi bocu votke i kutiju tableta te se nabo heroinom i po nekoliko dana ležao u komi, ali uvijek bi se probudio. Jednom se ljeti probudio s ustima punima mušica i mrava.

Kad su mu rekli da se žile režu po dužini, na zemlji je pronašao stari žilet. Bio je hrđav i prljav, pa ga je, uz crni humor, „dezinficirao“ pljuvačkom jer se bojao infekcije: „Ako ću već umirati, umrijet ću zdrav.“ Sjedeći na klupi, zarezao je lijevu ruku i otvorio ranu u koju je mogao gurnuti šaku. Dok je krv tekla, pomislio je samo: **„Hvala ti, Isuse, više je gotovo.“** Onesvijestio se i probudio u bolnici. „Koji jadnik, ne može se ni ubiti“, komentira.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uvjerljivo prenosi dubinu očaja i samoubilačkog pokušaja, ali izrazi da je smrt bila „spas“ i zahvala Isusu što je „više gotovo“ mogu, ako se shvate kao teološka tvrdnja, sugerirati da je smrt izbavljenje ili da Isus odobrava samoubojstvo. U kontekstu svjedočanstva riječ je prije o govoru čovjeka u krajnjoj patnji, no korisno je jasno razlikovati taj doživljaj od katoličkog nauka o vrijednosti života i nadi u Božje milosrđe.
concerns: Samoubojstvo se ne bi smjelo romantizirati kao spas niti se Isusu pripisivati odobravanje pokušaja; citirane riječi prenose očaj protagonista, a ne katolički nauk.
Podrugljivi komentar o tome da se nije uspio ubiti može pojačati samoprezir ili stigmu; odlomak bi bio pastoralno potpuniji kad bi naglasio ozbiljnost patnje i potrebu za ljudskom pomoći.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva samoubojstvo smatra teškim činom protiv života, ali istodobno priznaje da psihološki pritisci mogu umanjiti osobnu odgovornost te ne dopušta očajavati nad vječnim spasenjem onih koji su pokušali ili počinili samoubojstvo. Dikasterij opisuje očaj kao stanje koje može zatvoriti čovjekov pogled na budućnost i podsjeća na biblijski primjer Ilije, koji moli za smrt, ali prima pomoć da nastavi put; takva perspektiva dopušta ozbiljno govoriti o boli bez proglašavanja smrti rješenjem.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage convincingly conveys the depth of despair and the suicide attempt, but the expressions that death was “salvation” and the thanksgiving to Jesus that it was “finally over” can, if understood as a theological assertion, suggest that death is deliverance or that Jesus approves of suicide. In the context of testimony, this is rather the speech of a man in extreme suffering, but it is useful to distinguish clearly that experience from Catholic teaching on the value of life and hope in God's mercy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church considers suicide a grave act against life, but simultaneously recognizes that psychological pressures can diminish personal responsibility and does not allow despairing of the eternal salvation of those who have attempted or committed suicide. The Dicastery describes despair as a state that can close man's perspective on the future and recalls the biblical example of Elijah, who prays for death, but receives help to continue the journey; such a perspective allows one to speak seriously about pain without proclaiming death as the solution.
concerns_en: Suicide should not be romanticized as salvation, nor should approval of the attempt be attributed to Jesus; the quoted words convey the protagonist's despair, not Catholic teaching.

The mocking comment about how he failed to kill himself can intensify self-contempt or stigma; the passage would be pastorally more complete if it emphasized the seriousness of suffering and the need for human help.

sections.subtitle_en: Rock Bottom: When Death Looked Like Salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran speaks about the contempt of passersby and the desire for death
sections.content_en:
Goran could no longer sleep. He would carry a single sandwich in his pocket for twenty days or a month, and that was all his food. He was **full of live open wounds** and emitted a stench that, he says, listeners cannot even imagine. When he would enter a city bus, everyone would get off at the next stop, so he always had a place to sit.

He would sit huddled against a wall, and passersby spat on him, beat him with fists and feet, and shouted that he should be killed because he was **"poison for children."** To him it was all the same. He waited only for death because to him **death was salvation, and life was only suffering**. Countless times he would drink a bottle of vodka and a box of pills and shoot up with heroin and lie in a coma for several days, but he would always wake up. Once in the summer he woke up with his mouth full of flies and ants.

When they told him that veins are cut lengthwise, he found an old razor blade on the ground. It was rusty and dirty, so, with dark humor, he "disinfected" it with spit because he was afraid of infection: "If I'm going to die anyway, I'll die healthy." Sitting on a bench, he cut into his left arm and opened a wound into which he could push his fist. As the blood flowed, he thought only: **"Thank You, Jesus, it is finally over."** He passed out and woke up in the hospital. "What a wretched guy, he can't even kill himself," he comments.

sections.subtitle: Noć u polusrušenoj kućici i molitva Zdravo Marijo
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje trenutak kad je shvatio da je on sam kriv za svoj život
sections.content:
Jedne veljačke večeri Goran je ležao u polusrušenoj kućici, „kao pas na komadu kartona“, uz malu upaljenu svijeću. Počeo je razmišljati o obitelji i djetinjstvu, a što je više razmišljao, to ga je jače boljelo u prsima.

Na kraju je došao do ključne spoznaje: **nitko nije kriv, glavni krivac za sve je on sam**. Cijeli je život krivio druge, najviše obitelj, jer je morao kriviti druge kako bi opravdao zlo koje čini. Kad je shvatio da je on taj koji je sam sebi uništio život, počeo je plakati i moliti **Zdravo Marijo**.

Naglašava koliko je dotad mrzio Boga, Isusa, Gospu, Crkvu, svećenike i vjernike, tolikom mržnjom da je slušatelji ne mogu zamisliti. Zdravo Marijo bila je jedina molitva koja mu je ostala u sjećanju s vjeronauka na koji su ga roditelji tjerali. Cijelu je noć plakao i molio: „Gospe moja, uzmi me gore sebi ili mi pruži ruku da promijenim ovaj bijedni život. **Ja više ne mogu, umoran sam**, radi od mene što god hoćeš.“

magisterium.assessment: Priznanje vlastite krivnje i molitva u času slomljenosti uglavnom su u skladu s kršćanskim pokajanjem: ono čovjeka suočava s istinom o njegovu životu i otvara ga Božjem milosrđu. Molitva Zdravo Marijo također je katolički razumljiva kao obraćanje Mariji za majčinsko zagovorništvo, a ne kao zamjena za Boga ili Krista.
concerns: Tvrdnja da „nitko nije kriv” i da je on „glavni krivac za sve” može biti zdravo preuzimanje odgovornosti za vlastite postupke, ali bi bila teološki i ljudski problematična ako bi značila da tuđi grijesi ili nepravde nikada nisu postojali. Pokajanje nije isto što i poricanje tuđe odgovornosti ni samoprezir.
Molba da ga Gospa „uzme gore sebi” izražava duboku očajničku iscrpljenost i može zvučati kao želja za smrću; odlomak ne daje dovoljno osnove da se zaključi kako je riječ o čvrstoj namjeri ili nauku.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska ispovijed grijeha uključuje ponizno priznanje osobne krivnje, ali se odvija pred Bogom koji poznaje srce i čija je milost veća od čovjekove osude samoga sebe. Marijino zagovorništvo katolički se razumije kao majčinsko upućivanje Kristu: ona ne zauzima mjesto jedinoga Spasitelja, nego vjernike vodi prema njemu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The acknowledgment of personal guilt and prayer in the hour of brokenness are mainly in accordance with Christian repentance: it confronts man with the truth about his life and opens him to God's mercy. The Hail Mary prayer is likewise Catholically understandable as turning to Mary for maternal intercession, and not as a replacement for God or Christ.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian confession of sins includes a humble acknowledgment of personal guilt, but takes place before God who knows the heart and whose mercy is greater than man's self-condemnation. Mary's intercession is Catholically understood as maternally pointing toward Christ: she does not take the place of the sole Savior, but leads the faithful to him.
concerns_en: The assertion that “nobody is to blame” and that he is “the main culprit for everything” can be a healthy assumption of responsibility for one's own actions, but would be theologically and humanly problematic if it meant that others' sins or injustices never existed. Repentance is not the same as denying the responsibility of others or self-contempt.

The plea that Our Lady “take him up to herself” expresses deep, desperate exhaustion and can sound like a wish for death; the passage does not provide sufficient basis to conclude that this is a firm intention or teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: A Night in a Semi-Ruined Shack and the Hail Mary Prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes the moment when he realized that he himself was to blame for his life
sections.content_en:
One February evening Goran was lying in a semi-ruined shack, "like a dog on a piece of cardboard," beside a small lit candle. He began thinking about his family and childhood, and the more he thought, the more intensely it hurt in his chest.

In the end he came to a crucial realization: **no one is to blame, the main culprit for everything is he himself**. His whole life he blamed others, most of all his family, because he had to blame others to justify the evil he was doing. When he realized that he was the one who had destroyed his own life, he began to weep and pray the **Hail Mary**.

He emphasizes how much until then he had hated God, Jesus, Our Lady, the Church, priests, and believers, with such hatred that listeners cannot imagine it. The Hail Mary was the only prayer that remained in his memory from the catechism his parents had forced him to attend. All night he wept and prayed: "My Lady, take me up to yourself or extend your hand to me to change this wretched life. **I can't take it anymore, I am tired**, do with me whatever you want."

sections.subtitle: Žena u parku koja je tražila „Čuku“
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava susret sa ženom koja mu je u parku prišla s „problemom“
sections.content:
Nekoliko dana kasnije, rano jednog zimskog jutra, Goran je sjedio skupljen na klupi u parku kad je u park ušla žena i uputila se ravno prema njemu. Uz smijeh publike naglašava da „to nije bila Gospa“. Pozdravila ga je i zamolila za pomoć jer ima „jedan problem“. Goran se razbjesnio: zar ona njemu govori o problemu kad on ima toliko svojih? Grubo ju je otjerao.

Žena je tada rekla da traži mladića kojeg zovu **Čuke**, a to je bio Goranov nadimak na ulici. Bojao se da će, ako prizna, početi vikati, okupiti ljude i pozvati policiju, ali ga je svladala radoznalost. Kad je rekao „Ja sam“, žena je podigla glavu: „O, Gospe moja, hvala ti da sam ga našla.“ Goran je pomislio da nije normalna.

Uhvatila ga je pod ruku i pozvala u šetnju. Pristao je samo zato što je računao da će mu, kad ga već treba, dati novac, i dala mu ga je.

Tada je ispričala svoju priču. Majka je narkomana koji je završio u zatvoru i preko suda je izborila da sin kaznu služi u zajednici koju Goran naziva Černakolo. Pitala je sina ima li prijatelja kojemu bi mogla pomoći, a on je spomenuo Gorana. Goran ističe da u tome **nema nikakve logike**: mladić je deset godina mlađi od njega i s njim je samo dvaput uzeo heroin u jednoj drvarnici.

Žena, **Dijana**, u kratkom mu je vremenu izvadila osobnu iskaznicu i domovnicu jer nije imao nikakvih dokumenata. Zatim ga je odvela na autobusni kolodvor u Splitu i kupila mu kartu. Kad ju je upitao kamo ide, sretno je odgovorila: **„Gorane, ti ideš u Međugorje.“** Objasnila mu je da je to malo mjesto u Bosni i Hercegovini gdje se ukazuje Gospa, koja ga čeka, voli i pomoći će mu. Goran je pomislio: „Ja sam šizofreničar, ali ova je luđa od mene sto puta.“ Ipak je zaključio da je put besplatan, da je klošar može spavati bilo gdje i da je Međugorje udaljeno svega 150-ak kilometara, pa je krenuo „na izlet“.

magisterium.assessment: Susret s Dijanom, njezina konkretna pomoć i poziv na liječenje mogu se prikazati kao providonosni događaji koji otvaraju put obraćenju; takvo tumačenje je spojivo s katoličkom vjerom u Božju providnost i s kršćanskom dužnošću pomaganja potrebitima. Ipak, tvrdnju da se Gospa ukazuje u Međugorju i da ondje osobno čeka Gorana treba prepoznati kao Dijanino tumačenje, a ne kao nešto što ovaj odlomak sam po sebi dokazuje.
concerns: Prikaz može ostaviti dojam da su ukazanja u Međugorju potvrđena činjenica. Crkveno razlučivanje navodnih nadnaravnih pojava zahtijeva ispitivanje, a vjernike se potiče da ne usmjeruju pozornost pretjerano na izvanredne događaje nego na Krista, Božju riječ, molitvu, obraćenje i služenje bližnjima.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje providnosti dopušta da se obični ljudski susreti i djela pomoći promatraju kao moguća sredstva Božje skrbi, ali to ne znači da se svaki neobičan događaj može bez razlučivanja proglasiti nadnaravnim. U procjeni duhovnih pojava važni su, među ostalim, vjernost nauku, obraćenje, molitva, ljubav prema bližnjima i trajni duhovni plodovi.
