magisterium.assessment_en: The encounter with Dijana, her concrete help, and the invitation to treatment can be presented as providential events that open the way to conversion; such an interpretation is compatible with Catholic faith in God's providence and with the Christian duty to help those in need. Nevertheless, the claim that Our Lady is appearing in Međugorje and personally waiting for Goran there should be recognized as Dijana's interpretation, and not as something that this passage proves in itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of providence allows ordinary human encounters and acts of assistance to be viewed as potential means of God's care, but this does not mean that every unusual event can be declared supernatural without discernment. In evaluating spiritual phenomena, what is important includes, among other things, fidelity to doctrine, conversion, prayer, charity toward neighbors, and lasting spiritual fruits.
concerns_en: The presentation may leave the impression that the apparitions in Međugorje are a confirmed fact. Ecclesial discernment of alleged supernatural phenomena requires examination, and the faithful are encouraged not to focus their attention excessively on extraordinary events but on Christ, the Word of God, prayer, conversion, and service to neighbors.

sections.subtitle_en: The Woman in the Park Who Was Looking for "Čuke"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts the encounter with the woman who approached him in the park with a "problem"
sections.content_en:
A few days later, early one winter morning, Goran was sitting huddled on a bench in the park when a woman entered the park and headed straight toward him. To the laughter of the audience, he emphasizes that "it wasn't Our Lady." She greeted him and asked for help because she had "a problem." Goran became furious: is she talking to him about a problem when he has so many of his own? He rudely chased her away.

The woman then said she was looking for a young man called **Čuke**, which was Goran's nickname on the street. He was afraid that, if he admitted it, she would start screaming, gather people, and call the police, but curiosity overcame him. When he said "It's me," the woman raised her head: "Oh, my Lady, thank you that I found him." Goran thought she was out of her mind.

She took him by the arm and invited him for a walk. He agreed only because he calculated that, since she needed him, she would give him money, and she did give it to him.

Then she told her story. She was the mother of a drug addict who had ended up in prison, and through the court she had fought for her son to serve his sentence in a community that Goran calls Černakolo. She asked her son if he had a friend whom she could help, and he mentioned Goran. Goran emphasizes that **there is no logic in that**: the young man was ten years younger than him and had only twice taken heroin with him in a woodshed.

The woman, **Dijana**, in a short time obtained an identity card and certificate of citizenship for him because he had no documents at all. Then she took him to the bus station in Split and bought him a ticket. When he asked her where he was going, she happily replied: **"Goran, you are going to Međugorje."** She explained to him that it is a small town in Bosnia and Herzegovina where Our Lady appears, who is waiting for him, loves him, and will help him. Goran thought: "I'm a schizophrenic, but this woman is a hundred times crazier than me." Still, he concluded that the trip was free, that as a tramp he could sleep anywhere, and that Međugorje was only about 150 kilometers away, so he set off "on a trip."

sections.subtitle: Ulazak u zajednicu usred krize i otpor prema krunicama
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje svoju reakciju na svakodnevnu molitvu tri krunice u zajednici
sections.content:
Čim je izašao iz autobusa u Međugorju, Goran je u prvom dućanu **ukrao dvije litre vina** i popio ih. Lutajući mjestom došao je do kapije zajednice i sjetio se da mu je Dijana govorila o njoj. Mladići su ga primijetili, razgovarali s njim i odmah ga primili. To naziva čudom jer, kako kaže, **u zajednicu nitko nikad nije ušao u krizi**, a on jest, ni sam ne zna zašto.

Prvi mjesec apstinencijske krize bio je „nešto najgore u životu“: bez tableta, alkohola, cigareta, novina i televizije, samo težak rad i molitva. Mislio je da će umrijeti, no od krize, ističe, nitko nije umro. Odjeću koju su skinuli s njega nije bilo moguće oprati pa su je spalili. **Sestra Elvira** uplašila se, vidjevši ga punog otvorenih rana, da je u posljednjem stadiju side. Odmah su mu napravili sve pretrage i, „Bogu hvala“, nije bio zaražen. Kriza je prošla i polako je dolazio k sebi.

Najviše su ga živcirale **tri krunice koje se u zajednici mole svaki dan**. Govorio je da neće biti svećenik i da nema problem s molitvom, nego s alkoholom, drogom i tabletama. Kad ga je jedan mladić upitao hoće li moliti ili ne, nije htio biti bezobrazan prema onima koji su ga primili. Pristao je na jednu krunicu od 15 do 20 minuta, ali ne na tri. Mladići su odgovorili da će ostale dvije moliti oni za njega, što je on zadovoljno prihvatio. „Cijeli život mi je bio logičan, zato sam i završio gdje sam završio“, zaključuje uz smijeh.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem molitve i obraćenja: krunica se prikazuje kao praksa zajednice, a pripovjedačev otpor kao dio postupnog povratka, ne kao nauk protiv molitve. Ipak, tvrdnja da od apstinencijske krize „nitko nije umro” treba ostati osobno svjedočanstvo, a ne opće zdravstveno pravilo.
concerns: Ako se rečenica o tome da od apstinencijske krize nitko nije umro shvati kao medicinska tvrdnja za sve slučajeve, može umanjiti ozbiljnost apstinencijske krize; to nije teološki nauk i ne bi smjelo zamijeniti stručnu zdravstvenu procjenu.
Tri krunice dnevno prikazane su kao običaj te zajednice, a ne kao obveza svih katolika; ne bi ih trebalo predstavljati kao univerzalni crkveni propis.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica je marijanska molitva usmjerena na Krista: njezina je svrha razmatranje Kristovih otajstava i oblikovanje kršćanskog života, a ne puko ispunjavanje brojčane norme. U prikazu je zato važno što zajednica moli za Gorana i strpljivo mu ostavlja prostor da prihvati molitvu postupno; to je u skladu s razumijevanjem krunice kao duhovne pomoći, a ne čarobnog ili prisilnog čina.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Catholic understanding of prayer and conversion: the Rosary is presented as a community practice, and the narrator's resistance as part of a gradual return, not as a teaching against prayer. Nevertheless, the claim that “no one has died” from withdrawal should remain personal testimony, rather than a general health rule.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Rosary is a Marian prayer centered on Christ: its purpose is contemplation of the mysteries of Christ and the shaping of Christian life, rather than mere fulfillment of a numerical norm. In the account, it is therefore important that the community prays for Goran and patiently leaves him room to accept prayer gradually; this is in accordance with understanding the Rosary as spiritual assistance, rather than a magical or coercive act.
concerns_en: If the sentence that no one has died from withdrawal is understood as a medical claim for all cases, it can diminish the seriousness of withdrawal symptoms; this is not theological doctrine and should not replace professional medical evaluation.
Three Rosaries a day are presented as a custom of that community, not as an obligation for all Catholics; they should not be represented as a universal Church regulation.

sections.subtitle_en: Entering the Community in the Midst of Withdrawal and Resistance to Rosaries
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes his reaction to the daily prayer of three Rosaries in the community
sections.content_en:
As soon as he got off the bus in Međugorje, Goran **stole two liters of wine** in the first store and drank them. Wandering through the town, he came to the gate of the community and remembered that Dijana had spoken to him about it. The young men noticed him, talked with him, and took him in immediately. He calls that a miracle because, as he says, **no one ever entered the community in withdrawal**, but he did, without even knowing why himself.

The first month of withdrawal was "the worst thing in life": without pills, alcohol, cigarettes, newspapers, and television, only hard work and prayer. He thought he was going to die, but from withdrawal, he points out, no one has died. The clothes they took off him were impossible to wash, so they burned them. **Sister Elvira** was frightened, seeing him full of open wounds, that he was in the final stage of AIDS. They immediately ran all tests on him and, "thank God," he was not infected. The withdrawal passed and he slowly came to his senses.

What irritated him most were the **three Rosaries that are prayed in the community every day**. He said that he was not going to be a priest and that he did not have a problem with prayer, but with alcohol, drugs, and pills. When one young man asked him whether he would pray or not, he did not want to be rude to those who had taken him in. He agreed to one Rosary of 15 to 20 minutes, but not to three. The young men answered that they would pray the other two for him, which he gladly accepted. "My whole life was logical, that's why I ended up where I ended up," he concludes with laughter.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija iz kamenoloma: djela, a ne riječi
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje kako je sjedio u hladu dok su drugi za njega razbijali kamen
sections.content:
Goran zatim iznosi priču koju, kaže, nikome nije ispričao desetak godina. Bilo je ljeto, u Međugorju zna biti i 40 do 45 stupnjeva, a odgovorni u zajednici dao mu je **macolu od dvanaest kilograma** i poslao ga u kamenolom. Goran je odbio jer, kako je rekao, nije došao uništiti zdravlje.

Odgovorni mu je rekao da uzme stolicu i sjedne. Drugi mladić dodao je: „Ako ti nećeš raditi, mi ćemo raditi za tebe.“ Goran ih je nazvao budalama. Sjedio je u hladu na plastičnoj stolici, a oni su na žezi u rupi razbijali kamen, dok su im krhotine letjele „kao geleri“ i ranjavale ih. Mislio je da je to gore od koncentracijskog logora.

Nakon nekoliko dana počelo se događati nešto čudno. Mladići su teško radili, ali su bili **sretni: pjevali su, pričali viceve, molili se i šalili**. On nije radio ništa, a bio je ljut, nervozan i ljubomoran, „sve zlo na njemu“. Tada se zapitao tko je zapravo lud, oni koji rade ili on koji ne radi.

Zaključio je da je budala on jer je **prvi put u životu vidio da netko nešto radi za njega**. Shvatio je da u životu često nisu važne riječi, nego djela. Postidio se gledajući kako tovare kamione, ustao je i otišao raditi. Od tada mu se, kaže, život okrenuo.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja poruka — da se briga za drugoga očituje konkretnim djelima i da rad može postati služenje — dobro se slaže s kršćanskim naglaskom na solidarnosti, ljudskom dostojanstvu i djelatnoj ljubavi. No priča ne bi smjela sugerirati da su opasan fizički rad ili moguće ponižavanje prikladna terapija za svakoga, jer rad treba poštovati ljudsko dostojanstvo i služiti općem dobru.
concerns: Rad u velikoj žezi s macolom od dvanaest kilograma i letećim krhotinama opisuje stvarne rizike; bez dodatnih informacija ne može se zaključiti da su uvjeti bili sigurni ili prikladni za oporavak.
Usporedba s koncentracijskim logorom očita je pripovjedačeva hiperbola, ali može zvučati kao umanjivanje povijesne patnje ako se uzme doslovno.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje rada ne svodi ga na puku produktivnost: rad može sudjelovati u Božjem stvaralačkom djelu i služiti bližnjemu, ali njegova svrha mora biti dobro čovjeka i zajednice. Evanđeoski naglasak na služenju i velikodušnom dijeljenju plodova rada pomaže razumjeti zašto je Goranova promjena potaknuta time što su drugi radili za njega; ipak, taj duhovni plod ne opravdava zanemarivanje sigurnosti ili dostojanstva radnika.

magisterium.assessment_en: The central message — that care for another is manifested in concrete deeds and that work can become service — accords well with the Christian emphasis on solidarity, human dignity, and active love. However, the story should not suggest that hazardous physical labor or possible humiliation are appropriate therapy for everyone, because work must respect human dignity and serve the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of work does not reduce it to mere productivity: work can participate in God's creative work and serve one's neighbor, but its purpose must be the good of man and of the community. The gospel emphasis on service and generous sharing of the fruits of work helps explain why Goran's transformation was sparked by others working on his behalf; nevertheless, this spiritual fruit does not justify disregarding the safety or dignity of workers.
concerns_en: Work in intense heat with a twelve-kilogram sledgehammer and flying shards describes real risks; without additional information, it cannot be concluded that the conditions were safe or appropriate for recovery.
The comparison to a concentration camp is obvious narrator hyperbole, but it can sound like trivializing historical suffering if taken literally.

sections.subtitle_en: A Lesson from the Quarry: Deeds, Not Words
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes how he sat in the shade while others broke stone for him
sections.content_en:
Goran then shares a story that, he says, he had not told anyone for about ten years. It was summer, in Međugorje it can be 40 to 45 degrees, and the leader in the community gave him a **twelve-kilogram sledgehammer** and sent him to the quarry. Goran refused because, as he said, he did not come to ruin his health.

The leader told him to take a chair and sit down. Another young man added: "If you won't work, we will work for you." Goran called them fools. He sat in the shade on a plastic chair, and they broke stone in the heat in the pit, while splinters flew "like shrapnel" and wounded them. He thought that was worse than a concentration camp.

After a few days something strange began to happen. The young men worked hard, but they were **happy: they sang, told jokes, prayed, and joked around**. He was doing nothing, yet he was angry, nervous, and jealous, "all evil upon him." Then he wondered who was actually crazy, those who work or he who does not work.

He concluded that he was the fool because **for the first time in his life he saw someone doing something for him**. He realized that in life words are often not important, but deeds. He felt ashamed watching them load the trucks, he stood up and went to work. From then on, he says, his life turned around.

sections.subtitle: Molitva u dva ujutro i zagrljaj oca u blagovaonici
sections.screenshot_description: Goran emotivno prepričava neočekivani susret s ocem i njihov zagrljaj
sections.content:
Nakon jedanaest mjeseci u zajednici u Goranu je rasla **ljubomora koja se pretvarala u mržnju** prema drugim mladićima: njima su dolazile obitelji, a njemu nitko. S obitelji nije imao kontakta deset godina, devet na ulici i godinu u zajednici. Kroz svakodnevnu molitvu savjest mu je ipak sve više rasla. Bilo mu je žao svega što je učinio i htio se pomiriti s obitelji i ocem.

Planirao je napisati pismo, ali su mu mladići rekli da mora prinijeti žrtvu jer **„bez žrtve nema ljubavi i nema plodova“**. Savjetovali su mu da svako jutro ustaje u dva sata, ide u kapelu i ondje sat vremena kleči, moli i vjeruje. Nije mu se dalo, ali je želja za pomirenjem bila jača pa je počeo ustajati, klečati i moliti. Priznaje da nije vjerovao jer je bio siguran da će prije umrijeti nego što će se otac pomiriti s njim.

Nije prošao ni mjesec kada ga je jedan mladić zamolio da hodočasnicima iz Hrvatske pokaže zajednicu. Otvorio je vrata blagovaonice, podigao glavu i prvo lice koje je ugledao bilo je **očevo**. Odmah je spustio pogled. Osjećaj srama i krivnje opisuje kao najteži trenutak u životu i nije imao hrabrosti ponovno pogledati oca. Otac je vidio koliko mu je teško, prišao mu, **zagrlio ga i zaplakao**. Goran je zagrlio njega i oni su cijeli dan samo plakali, bez riječi.

Nije znao što bi rekao. Nije mogao ni tražiti oprost jer nije bio siguran da će uspjeti, a nakon života punog laži prvi je put htio biti pošten i ne davati lažnu nadu. Kad je otac odlazio, rekao mu je da je uništio i sebe i njih, da ne može ništa obećati i da se možda sutra vrati na staru cestu. Zamolio ga je samo za jedno: da sa svojom ženom počne moliti za njegovo obraćenje.

Otac ga je pogledao i odgovorio: **„Sinko, pa mi se već dugo godina za tebe molimo.“** Goran danas smatra da je sve tako trebalo biti kako bi se molitva i vjera vratile u njegovu obitelj. Svatko, kaže, ima svoj križni put kojim mu Bog daje do znanja da se mora vratiti Crkvi, a sva ta patnja i bol imale su smisla.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na molitvi, obraćenju, kajanju i pomirenju: očev zagrljaj prikazuje milosrđe, a Goranova iskrenost priznaje da oprost ne uklanja automatski posljedice prošlosti. Ipak, tvrdnju da Bog svakome daje križni put kako bi ga vratio Crkvi treba razumjeti kao osobno svjedočanstvo o pronađenom smislu patnje, a ne kao opće pravilo o tome zašto ljudi pate.
concerns: Izreka „bez žrtve nema ljubavi i nema plodova“ može biti pobožan poticaj na odricanje, ali izrečena bez pojašnjenja zvuči apsolutno: ljubav i duhovni plodovi prvenstveno su dar Božje milosti, a ne nagrada za određenu količinu samonametnute patnje.

Tvrdnju da Bog svakome daje križni put kako bi ga vratio Crkvi valja oprezno tumačiti. Katolički pogled dopušta da Bog patnju preobrazi i iz nje izvede dobro, ali ne opravdava zaključak da Bog svako zlo ili bol neposredno šalje radi obraćenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Molitva i ustrajnost mogu čovjeka osposobiti za obraćenje i pomirenje; katolički nauk ističe da se smisao patnje postupno otkriva u svjetlu Kristove muke i uskrsnuća, a ne da svaka patnja odmah ima očito objašnjenje. Očev odgovor također naglašava važnost molitve obitelji, dok njegovo prihvaćanje sina pokazuje mogućnost novog početka bez poricanja počinjene štete.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Catholic emphasis on prayer, conversion, repentance, and reconciliation: the father's embrace depicts mercy, and Goran's honesty acknowledges that forgiveness does not automatically remove the consequences of the past. Nevertheless, the claim that God gives everyone a Way of the Cross in order to bring them back to the Church should be understood as personal testimony about meaning found in suffering, rather than as a general rule regarding why people suffer.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Prayer and perseverance can equip a person for conversion and reconciliation; Catholic teaching emphasizes that the meaning of suffering is gradually revealed in the light of Christ's passion and resurrection, and not that every suffering immediately has an obvious explanation. The father's response also highlights the importance of family prayer, while his acceptance of the son demonstrates the possibility of a new beginning without denying the harm committed.
concerns_en: The saying “without sacrifice there is no love and there are no fruits” can be a pious encouragement toward self-denial, but stated without clarification it sounds absolute: love and spiritual fruits are primarily a gift of God's grace, and not a reward for a certain amount of self-imposed suffering.

The claim that God gives everyone a Way of the Cross in order to bring them back to the Church should be interpreted cautiously. The Catholic view allows that God transforms suffering and brings good out of it, but does not justify the conclusion that God directly sends every evil or pain for the sake of conversion.

sections.subtitle_en: Prayer at Two in the Morning and a Father's Embrace in the Dining Hall
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran emotionally recounts the unexpected encounter with his father and their embrace
sections.content_en:
After eleven months in the community, in Goran grew a **jealousy that turned into hatred** toward the other young men: their families came to visit them, but no one came to him. He had had no contact with his family for ten years, nine on the street and one in the community. Through daily prayer, however, his conscience grew more and more. He was sorry for everything he had done and wanted to reconcile with his family and father.

He planned to write a letter, but the young men told him that he had to offer a sacrifice because **"without sacrifice there is no love and there are no fruits."** They advised him to get up every morning at two o'clock, go to the chapel, and kneel, pray, and believe there for an hour. He didn't feel like it, but the desire for reconciliation was stronger, so he began getting up, kneeling, and praying. He admits that he did not believe because he was sure he would die before his father would reconcile with him.

Not even a month had passed when a young man asked him to show pilgrims from Croatia around the community. He opened the dining hall door, raised his head, and the first face he saw was **his father's**. He immediately lowered his gaze. He describes the feeling of shame and guilt as the hardest moment in his life, and he did not have the courage to look at his father again. His father saw how hard it was for him, approached him, **embraced him, and wept**. Goran embraced him, and they just wept all day, without words.

He did not know what to say. He could not even ask for forgiveness because he was not sure he would succeed, and after a life full of lies, for the first time he wanted to be honest and not give false hope. When his father was leaving, he told him that he had destroyed both himself and them, that he could promise nothing, and that maybe tomorrow he would return to the old path. He asked him for only one thing: to begin praying with his wife for his conversion.

His father looked at him and answered: **"Son, we have already been praying for you for many years."** Goran today believes that everything was meant to be that way so that prayer and faith would return to his family. Everyone, he says, has their own Way of the Cross by which God lets them know that they must return to the Church, and all that suffering and pain had meaning.

sections.subtitle: „Napravit ću od tebe direktora“: novi početak u Međugorju
sections.screenshot_description: Goran Ćurković prepričava obećanje fratra da će od njega napraviti 'direktora'
sections.content:
Susret s ocem u zajednici, nakon kojeg su obojica cijeli dan samo plakala, **Goran Ćurković** opisuje kao prekretnicu. Taj mu je trenutak dao još jaču želju, nadu i volju da se obrati i da u zajednici ustraje. **Nakon četiri godine odlučuje izaći van.** U Split se nije želio vratiti jer se, kako kaže, u Međugorju osjećao „ponovo rođen“.

Izlazak je donio nov i vrlo praktičan problem: nitko mu nije htio dati posao i nitko mu nije vjerovao. Goran priznaje da se pitao što će bez posla raditi i hoće li ponovno krasti. Odgovor mu je bio jasan: želio je živjeti pošteno, kao i drugi ljudi. Zato se, kaže, počeo još više moliti, a „Gospa je riješila“.

Rješenje je došlo preko pokojnog **fra Slavka Barbarića**, fratra kojeg Goran naziva legendom Međugorja i koji je umro na Križevcu. Fra Slavko je u zajednicu dolazio ispovijedati, voditi klanjanja i svaki dan služiti misu, a Goran je s njim bio u dobrim odnosima. Povjerio mu se da ne želi cijeli život provesti u zajednici, da se ne želi vratiti u Split i da želi početi „iz nule“, ostajući živjeti „ovdje s Gospom“.

Fratar mu je odgovorio da ga već dugo prati, da vidi kako je dobar momak i da će mu nešto naći, ali da mora biti strpljiv. Nije prošlo ni dvadeset dana, a fra Slavko je došao s „radosnom vijesti“. Imao je posao, uz upozorenje: „Nemoj me razočarati… Gorane, vjeruj mi, napravit ću od tebe direktora.“

Goran se publici duhovito prisjeća svojih tadašnjih misli: ispalo je da se „isplatilo drogirati“, jer bez toga nikad ne bi postao direktor. Kad je ostao sam, nije mu bilo jasno kako bi on, bez škole i bez ičega, „obični narkoman“, mogao biti direktor. Fratar pak nije mogao lagati, „a pogotovo svećenik“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno usklađen s katoličkim pouzdanjem u molitvu, providnost, pošten rad i mogućnost novog početka nakon obraćenja. Humorističku primjedbu da se „isplatilo drogirati“ treba shvatiti kao retrospektivnu šalu, a ne kao tvrdnju da je ovisnost dobra ili da je zlo nužno za postizanje dobra.
concerns: Šala o tome da se drogiranje „isplatilo“ može, odvojena od konteksta, zvučati kao opravdavanje ovisnosti; teološki je važno razlikovati dobro koje Bog može izvesti iz prošlih grijeha i zla od samoga grijeha, koji time ne postaje dobar ni poželjan.

Izraz „Gospa je riješila“ prihvatljiv je kao sažet govor o pouzdanju u Marijin zagovor, ali ne bi ga trebalo razumjeti kao da Marija djeluje neovisno o Bogu ili kao da molitva jamči određeni posao ili uspjeh.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pogled na providnost dopušta da molitva prati praktične napore i da se dobro ostvari kroz ljude i okolnosti, bez zaključka da je svaki pojedini ishod zajamčen. Izlazak iz zajednice i traženje posla prikazani su kao nastavak odgovornog života, a ne kao zamjena za obraćenje; Goranova prošlost može postati dio svjedočanstva o milosti, ali ne i razlog za romantiziranje droge ili krađe.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is predominantly aligned with Catholic trust in prayer, providence, honest work, and the possibility of a new beginning after conversion. The humorous remark that “doing drugs paid off” should be understood as a retrospective joke, rather than as a claim that addiction is good or that evil is necessary to achieve good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic view of providence allows prayer to accompany practical efforts and good to be realized through people and circumstances, without concluding that every single outcome is guaranteed. Leaving the community and seeking employment are presented as a continuation of a responsible life, rather than as a replacement for conversion; Goran's past can become part of a testimony of grace, but not a reason to romanticize drugs or theft.
concerns_en: The joke about doing drugs “paying off” can, detached from context, sound like justifying addiction; theologically, it is important to distinguish the good that God can bring out of past sins and evil from sin itself, which does not thereby become good or desirable.

The expression “Our Lady handled it” is acceptable as shorthand for trust in Mary's intercession, but it should not be understood as though Mary acts independently of God or as though prayer guarantees a specific job or success.

sections.subtitle_en: "I Will Make a Director Out of You": A New Beginning in Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran Ćurković recounts the friar's promise that he would make a 'director' out of him
sections.content_en:
The encounter with his father in the community, after which both just wept all day, **Goran Ćurković** describes as a turning point. That moment gave him an even stronger desire, hope, and will to convert and to persevere in the community. **After four years he decides to go out.** He did not want to return to Split because, as he says, in Međugorje he felt "born again."

Going out brought a new and very practical problem: no one wanted to give him a job and no one trusted him. Goran admits that he wondered what he would do without a job and whether he would steal again. The answer was clear to him: he wanted to live honestly, like other people. That is why, he says, he began praying even more, and "Our Lady resolved it."

The solution came through the late **fra Slavko Barbarić**, a friar whom Goran calls a legend of Međugorje and who died on Križevac. Fra Slavko came to the community to hear confessions, lead Eucharistic adoration, and celebrate Mass every day, and Goran was on good terms with him. He confided in him that he did not want to spend his whole life in the community, that he did not want to return to Split, and that he wanted to start "from scratch," remaining to live "here with Our Lady."

The friar answered him that he had been observing him for a long time, that he saw he was a good guy, and that he would find something for him, but that he had to be patient. Not even twenty days had passed, and fra Slavko came with "good news." He had a job, with a warning: "Don't disappoint me… Goran, trust me, I will make a director out of you."

Goran humorously recalls to the audience his thoughts at the time: it turned out that "it paid off to do drugs," because without that he would never have become a director. When he was left alone, it was not clear to him how he, without education and without anything, "an ordinary junkie," could be a director. The friar, however, could not lie, "and especially not a priest."

sections.subtitle: „Direktor zahoda“ i prozor koji gleda na vrata
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje prozor 'direktorske kancelarije' kraj toaleta iza crkve
sections.content:
Kad je došao u župni ured i pitao što će raditi, fra Slavko mu je kratko odgovorio: „A čistiš zahode, a šta si mislio?“ Goran je u sebi zaključio da je postao **„direktor zahoda“**. Riječ je o toaletima za hodočasnike odmah iza crkve u Međugorju, s muškim i ženskim kabinama i umivaonicima. Posla je, kaže, bilo „do ovdje“.

Unatoč tome, posao mu se svidio. Čistio je, pjevao, molio se i upoznavao ljude, jer je „na zahodu stalno živo“. S vremenom je ipak postajao sve nervozniji. Radio je svaki dan, subotom, nedjeljom i blagdanima, od sedam ujutro do jedanaest navečer. Ni minute nije imao slobodno, a doručak, ručak i večeru donosile su mu časne sestre ravno na posao.

Goran naglašava da se ne žali. Takav ritam imao je i dobru stranu: plaću nije stigao potrošiti, pa je sav novac mogao štedjeti. Zahod nije morao plaćati jer je, šali se, kao direktor imao privilegije. Smetala ga je jedna stvar: **htio je pronaći djevojku**, a kako je naći kad je po cijeli dan na zahodu? Zaključio je da mu jedino preostaje „ljubav svoga života“ tražiti na javnom toaletu.

Objašnjava i jedan važan detalj. Danas toaleti imaju dva ulaza, ali u njegovo vrijeme postojala su samo jedna, muška vrata. Svi su ulazili kroz njih i tek se unutra razdvajali. Točno nasuprot tih vrata bila je „direktorska kancelarija“ s prozorom koji gleda na ulaz. Goran priznaje da je cijeli dan stajao iza tog prozora i promatrao cure. Pritom ga nije zanimalo tko je platio, a tko nije, pa je, kako se šali, župni ured bankrotirao jer nisu imali ni za papir.

I onda se dogodilo. U toalet je ušla mlada djevojka, a kad je prolazila pokraj njega, osjetio je kao da ga je „grom pukao u glavu“. Prvi ju je put vidio u životu i ništa o njoj nije znao, ali je u tom trenutku bio siguran: **„Gospa mi je dala na put, ona je moja.“**

magisterium.assessment: Molitva, rad i humor u prikazu sami po sebi nisu protivni katoličkom nauku, ali promatranje djevojaka kroz prozor i zaključak da mu je Gospa djevojku dala te da je ona njegova mogu zvučati kao svođenje osobe na predmet vlastite želje. To je osobno svjedočanstvo i šala, a ne nužno formalna tvrdnja o nauku ili objava, no valjalo bi jasnije ostaviti prostor njezinoj slobodi i vlastitom pozivu.
concerns: Promatranje žena bez njihova znanja, ako je opis doslovan, može biti nepoštovanje njihove privatnosti i dostojanstva.
Izraz da je ona njegova može zvučati posesivno; katoličko razumijevanje muškarca i žene polazi od jednake osobne vrijednosti, a ne od toga da je jedna osoba posjed druge.

Pripisivanje susreta Gospi kao sigurnog znaka da je djevojka određena baš za njega nadilazi ono što se može zaključiti iz samog susreta; za razlučivanje Božje volje potrebni su razboritost i poštovanje istine, a ne samo snažan dojam.
Opis rada svakoga dana od ranog jutra do kasne večeri bez odmora, ako je doslovan, izaziva pitanje poštovanja dostojanstva radnika; iz odlomka se ipak ne mogu utvrditi svi uvjeti rada.
magisterium.enrichment: Knjiga Postanka predstavlja muškarca i ženu kao osobe jednake dostojanstva, pozvane na uzajamnost, a ne kao nekoga tko drugoga može unaprijed prisvojiti. Katolička pobožnost prema Mariji ne zamjenjuje slobodno i razborito razlučivanje: njezina vjera pokazuje otvorenost Božjem pozivu, a ne pravo na drugu osobu. U prikazu je moguće prepoznati humor i osobni doživljaj, ali te izraze ne treba uzeti kao dokaz da je Bog zajamčio ishod.
magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer, work, and humor in the account are not in themselves contrary to Catholic teaching, but observing girls through a window and concluding that Our Lady gave him the girl and that she is his can sound like reducing a person to an object of one's own desire. This is personal testimony and a joke, rather than necessarily a formal doctrinal claim or revelation, but space should be more clearly left for her freedom and her own vocation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Book of Genesis presents man and woman as persons of equal dignity, called to reciprocity, rather than as someone whom another can preemptively appropriate. Catholic devotion to Mary does not replace free and prudent discernment: her faith demonstrates openness to God's call, not an entitlement to another person. In the presentation, it is possible to recognize humor and personal experience, but those expressions should not be taken as proof that God guaranteed the outcome.
concerns_en: Observing women without their knowledge, if the description is literal, can be disrespectful of their privacy and dignity.
The expression that she is his can sound possessive; the Catholic understanding of man and woman starts from equal personal worth, rather than one person being the possession of another.

Attributing the encounter to Our Lady as a certain sign that the girl was intended specifically for him goes beyond what can be concluded from the encounter itself; discerning God's will requires prudence and respect for truth, and not merely a strong impression.

The description of working every day from early morning until late evening without rest, if literal, raises the question of respecting worker dignity; nevertheless, all working conditions cannot be ascertained from the passage.

sections.subtitle_en: The "Director of Toilets" and the Window Looking at the Door
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes the window of the 'director's office' near the toilets behind the church
sections.content_en:
When he came to the parish office and asked what he would be doing, fra Slavko answered him briefly: "Why, you clean the toilets, what did you think?" Goran concluded to himself that he had become the **"director of toilets."** These were the toilets for pilgrims right behind the church in Međugorje, with men's and women's stalls and washbasins. There was, he says, work "up to here."

Despite that, he liked the job. He cleaned, sang, prayed, and met people, because "at the toilet it's constantly lively." Over time, however, he became increasingly nervous. He worked every day, on Saturdays, Sundays, and feast days, from seven in the morning until eleven at night. He didn't have a minute free, and breakfast, lunch, and dinner were brought to him by nuns straight to work.

Goran emphasizes that he is not complaining. Such a rhythm also had a good side: he didn't have time to spend his salary, so he could save all the money. He didn't have to pay for the toilet because, he jokes, as a director he had privileges. One thing bothered him: **he wanted to find a girlfriend**, and how to find one when he is at the toilet all day? He concluded that his only remaining option was to look for the "love of his life" in a public restroom.

He also explains an important detail. Today the toilets have two entrances, but in his time there was only one, men's door. Everyone entered through it and only separated inside. Directly opposite that door was the "director's office" with a window looking at the entrance. Goran admits that he stood behind that window all day and watched girls. At the same time he didn't care who paid and who didn't, so, as he jokes, the parish office went bankrupt because they didn't even have money for paper.

And then it happened. A young girl entered the restroom, and when she passed by him, he felt as if "lightning struck him in the head." He saw her for the first time in his life and knew nothing about her, but at that moment he was sure: **"Our Lady put her on my path, she is mine."**

sections.subtitle: Molitva za slobodno vrijeme i nepremostive prepreke
sections.screenshot_description: Goran nabraja svoje dijagnoze i prošlost uspoređujući se s djevojkom
sections.content:
Zbog posla Goran nije mogao krenuti za djevojkom ni raspitati se tko je i odakle je. Imao je problem koji sam nije mogao riješiti, a u takvim situacijama, kaže, ostaje samo **molitva**. Počeo se ponizno moliti Duhu Svetom da siđe na fratre i da mu oni promijene posao.

Nije prošlo ni deset dana, a pokojni **fra Ivan Bradvica** rekao mu je da je bio dobar na toaletima i da dobiva „unapređenje“. Kad je Goran oduševljeno došao u župni ured, saznao je da je novo radno mjesto metla: postao je čistač ulica po Međugorju. Bio je sretan, jer je sada radio osam sati i imao puno slobodnog vremena. Ističe da se nije molio za bolji posao ni za novac, nego upravo za slobodno vrijeme, kako bi saznao tko je ta djevojka.

Čim se počeo raspitivati, nastali su problemi. Otkrio je da je djevojka:

- **Čehinja** koja ne zna hrvatski,
- **trinaest godina mlađa** od njega,
- nikad nije imala momka,
- u Međugorje je došla moliti se za svoj poziv jer je **htjela postati časna sestra**.

Nasuprot tome Goran je stavio sebe, nabrajajući: narkoman, alkoholičar, ovisnik o tabletama, lopov, izrezan, istetoviran, s metkom u glavi, epilepsijom, shizofrenijom i hepatitisom C. Za kraj je dodao da je, kad bi se nasmijao, imao tri zuba, „dva siva i jedan crni“. Publiku je nasmijao pitanjem: „Koji ljepotan, koja me ne bi htjela?“

Prijatelji u Međugorju bili su manje šaljivi. Govorili su mu da nije nimalo ozdravio, da ga s takvim dijagnozama nitko nikad neće uzeti i da će cijeli život živjeti sam. Goran je ipak bio siguran da će ona biti njegova, iako je znao da neće ići jednostavno.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva Duhu Svetomu za pomoć u konkretnoj teškoći u skladu je s kršćanskim životom, a opis ne tvrdi da je unapređenje čudesno niti da su molitve obvezale fratre na određenu odluku. Ipak, sigurnost da će djevojka biti njegova može postati teološki problem ako se shvati kao Božje obećanje ili ako zanemaruje njezinu slobodu i razlučivanje redovničkog poziva.
concerns: Rečenica da će ona biti njegova može zvučati kao unaprijed zajamčen ishod, premda tekst ne pokazuje je li to samo izraz nade ili tvrdnja o Božjoj volji.
Djevojčin mogući redovnički poziv prikazan je kao prepreka njegovoj želji, pa je važno ne zanemariti da i ona ima vlastiti poziv i slobodu odlučivanja.
Nabrajanje ovisnosti i dijagnoza samo po sebi nije naukovna tvrdnja; iz odlomka se ne može prosuditi jesu li navedena stanja bila liječena, izliječena ili samo dio ranijeg života.
magisterium.enrichment: Pozivanje Duha Svetoga u molitvi ima čvrsto mjesto u kršćanskoj praksi; crkveni nauk potiče vjernike da ga zazivaju i traže da ih vodi prema istini. No razlučivanje ne znači tumačiti svaku želju ili povoljan događaj kao potvrdu unaprijed željenog ishoda: potrebno je ostati otvoren Božjoj volji i poštovati slobodu drugih. Samoponižavajući humor o bolesti i izgledu može pripadati osobnom svjedočanstvu, ali ne smije sugerirati da dijagnoze ili prošli grijesi umanjuju nečije ljudsko dostojanstvo.
magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer to the Holy Spirit for help in a specific difficulty is in accordance with Christian life, and the description does not claim that the promotion was miraculous nor that the prayers obligated the friars to make a specific decision. Nevertheless, the certainty that the girl would be his can become a theological problem if understood as a divine promise or if it disregards her freedom and discernment of a religious vocation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Invoking the Holy Spirit in prayer has a firm place in Christian practice; Church teaching encourages the faithful to invoke Him and ask Him to guide them toward truth. But discernment does not mean interpreting every desire or favorable event as confirmation of a pre-determined desired outcome: it is necessary to remain open to God's will and respect the freedom of others. Self-deprecating humor about illness and appearance can belong to personal testimony, but must not suggest that diagnoses or past sins diminish someone's human dignity.
concerns_en: The sentence that she will be his can sound like a predetermined guaranteed outcome, although the text does not show whether this is merely an expression of hope or a claim about God's will.
The girl's potential religious vocation is presented as an obstacle to his desire, so it is important not to overlook that she too has her own calling and freedom of decision.
Listing addictions and diagnoses in itself is not a doctrinal claim; from the passage it cannot be judged whether the stated conditions were treated, cured, or merely part of earlier life.

sections.subtitle_en: Prayer for Free Time and Insurmountable Obstacles
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran lists his diagnoses and past, comparing himself with the girl
sections.content_en:
Because of work, Goran could not go after the girl or inquire about who she was and where she was from. He had a problem that he could not solve on his own, and in such situations, he says, only **prayer** remains. He began to pray humbly to the Holy Spirit to descend upon the friars and have them change his job.

Not even ten days had passed, and the late **fra Ivan Bradvica** told him that he had been good at the toilets and that he was getting a "promotion." When Goran came enthusiastically to the parish office, he found out that his new workplace was a broom: he became a street sweeper throughout Međugorje. He was happy, because now he worked eight hours and had plenty of free time. He emphasizes that he did not pray for a better job or for money, but precisely for free time, in order to find out who that girl was.

As soon as he began inquiring, problems arose. He discovered that the girl was:

- a **Czech** who did not know Croatian,
- **thirteen years younger** than him,
- had never had a boyfriend,
- had come to Međugorje to pray for her vocation because **she wanted to become a nun**.

In contrast to that, Goran set himself, listing: junkie, alcoholic, pill addict, thief, cut up, tattooed, with a bullet in the head, epilepsy, schizophrenia, and hepatitis C. For the end he added that, when he smiled, he had three teeth, "two gray and one black." He made the audience laugh with the question: "What a handsome man, which woman wouldn't want me?"

Friends in Međugorje were less joking. They told him that he hadn't healed at all, that with such diagnoses no one would ever take him, and that he would live alone his whole life. Goran was nevertheless sure that she would be his, even though he knew it would not go simply.

sections.subtitle: Devet mjeseci „vjernog psa“ i lukavi plan s Hamburgom
sections.screenshot_description: Goran objašnjava promjenu taktike i izmišljeni odlazak u Njemačku
sections.content:
Sljedećih **devet mjeseci** Goran je, kako sam kaže, „kao pas“ trčao za djevojkom. Ona mu je govorila da je ružan, star i dosadan, ponižavala ga pred drugima i bila zla prema njemu. On je ipak, poput vjernog psa, i dalje hodao za njom.

Djevojka je živjela i radila u jednom pansionu kako bi imala sobu i mogla se moliti za svoj poziv. Goran se brzo sprijateljio s vlasnicima pansiona i ondje dolazio s čokoladama, bombonijerama i cvijećem. Kad bi ga vidjela, ona bi pobjegla i zaključala se u sobu. Rezultat devet mjeseci truda bio je, kako kaže, „ni milimetar“.

Tada je odlučio **promijeniti taktiku**. U pansionu je zatekao djevojku, koja se zvala **Katarina**, kako pere suđe. Sjeo je i rekao joj da je ovih dana bio u Njemačkoj, ondje upoznao djevojku koja ga želi, te da uzima svoje stvari i odlazi u Hamburg, gdje će se oženiti i imati obitelj i djecu. Dodao je i provokativno: „A ti peri suđe po Međugorju kad si glupa.“

Dok je to govorio, Katarina je bacila suđe i potrčala prema sobi. Goran je gledao za njom i pomislio: „Aha, bit će ovdje nešto.“ Ustao je i otišao.

Objašnjava i što se događalo s druge strane. Kroz tih devet mjeseci Katarina je upoznala kakav je on čovjek iznutra i počela osjećati simpatiju prema njemu, ali se bojala njegove prošlosti, što Goran smatra posve normalnim. Sada je bila tužna jer je mislila da odlazi i da se više nikad neće vidjeti. Htjela mu je otvoriti srce, reći što osjeća i zatražiti oprost, ali nije znala je li to Božja volja.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ne promiče pouzdano kršćansku ljubav: Goran nastavlja udvaranje unatoč njezinu izbjegavanju, vrijeđa je i namjerno izmišlja priču o odlasku i drugoj djevojci kako bi izazvao reakciju. Takva obmana i ponižavanje ozbiljno su nespojivi s istinoljubivošću i poštovanjem osobe, iako sam prikaz ne mora značiti da ih podcast moralno odobrava.
concerns: Laž o Njemačkoj i drugoj djevojci nije tek bezazlena dosjetka: služi manipuliranju Katarininim osjećajima, a Katekizam izričito kaže da prijateljstvo ni želja za postizanjem cilja ne opravdavaju dvoličan govor.

Njezino bježanje i zatvaranje u sobu upućuju na to da Goranovo uporno praćenje nije prikazano kao uzajamno udvaranje; vrijeđanje i omalovažavanje dodatno narušavaju dostojanstvo i dobrotu koje bi trebale obilježavati odnos.
Goranovo naknadno tumačenje da će njezina reakcija značiti kako „ima nešto“ može romantizirati taktiku pritiska, umjesto da ozbiljno uzme njezine riječi i granice.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska ljubav ne opravdava neistinito sredstvo ni zato što se želi postići poželjan ishod: istina i povjerenje čuvaju ljudske odnose, dok laž narušava njihovu osnovu. U zdravom udvaranju ustrajnost treba biti spojena s poštovanjem slobode druge osobe; nadimak „vjerni pas“ ne pretvara ponižavanje, obmanu ili ignoriranje odbijanja u krepost.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage does not reliably promote Christian love: Goran continues his courtship despite her avoidance, insults her, and deliberately invents a story about leaving and another girl to provoke a reaction. Such deceit and belittling are gravely incompatible with truthfulness and respect for the person, even though the depiction itself does not necessarily mean that the podcast morally approves of them.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian love does not justify untrue means even when seeking to achieve a desirable outcome: truth and trust safeguard human relationships, whereas lying undermines their foundation. In healthy courtship, perseverance must be combined with respect for the freedom of the other person; the nickname “faithful dog” does not turn belittling, deceit, or ignoring rejection into virtue.
concerns_en: The lie about Germany and another girl is not merely a harmless quip: it serves to manipulate Katarina's feelings, and the Catechism explicitly states that neither friendship nor the desire to attain a goal justifies deceitful speech.

Her fleeing and locking herself in a room indicate that Goran's persistent following is not portrayed as mutual courtship; insulting and belittling further harm the dignity and goodness that should characterize a relationship.
Goran's subsequent interpretation that her reaction would mean “there's something there” can romanticize pressure tactics, instead of taking her words and boundaries seriously.

sections.subtitle_en: Nine Months of a "Faithful Dog" and a Clever Plan with Hamburg
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran explains the change of tactics and the invented departure for Germany
sections.content_en:
For the next **nine months** Goran, as he says himself, ran after the girl "like a dog." She told him he was ugly, old, and annoying, humiliated him in front of others, and was mean to him. He nevertheless, like a faithful dog, continued walking after her.

The girl lived and worked in a guesthouse in order to have a room and be able to pray for her vocation. Goran quickly became friends with the owners of the guesthouse and came there with chocolates, boxes of chocolates, and flowers. When she saw him, she would run away and lock herself in her room. The result of nine months of effort was, as he says, "not a millimeter."

Then he decided to **change tactics**. In the guesthouse he found the girl, whose name was **Katarina**, washing dishes. He sat down and told her that he had been in Germany these days, had met a girl there who wanted him, and that he was taking his things and leaving for Hamburg, where he would get married and have a family and children. He also added provocatively: "And you keep washing dishes around Međugorje since you're stupid."

While he was saying that, Katarina threw down the dishes and ran toward her room. Goran watched after her and thought: "Aha, there will be something here." He got up and left.

He also explains what was happening on the other side. Through those nine months Katarina had gotten to know what kind of man he was on the inside and began to feel affection toward him, but she was afraid of his past, which Goran considers completely normal. Now she was sad because she thought he was leaving and they would never see each other again. She wanted to open her heart to him, tell what she felt, and ask for forgiveness, but she did not know whether that was God's will.

sections.subtitle: „Želiš li mi nešto reći?“: dogovor s Isusom na Križevcu
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava trenutak u kafiću kad je Katarini postavio ključno pitanje
sections.content:
Ne znajući što učiniti, Katarina je otišla na **Križevac**. Ondje je kleknula pod križ i, kako Goran prepričava, rekla Isusu da je tužna jer Goran odlazi, da Isus zna što osjeća prema njemu, ali da ne zna je li njegova volja da mu otvori srce. Zato je predložila „dogovor“: ako joj Goran te večeri sam od sebe postavi točno pitanje **„Želiš li mi nešto reći?“**, to će joj biti znak Božje volje i tada će mu sve reći.

Te je večeri Goran ušao u kafić na kavu i ugledao Katarinu s dvije prijateljice. Odmah je uzeo stolicu, sjeo do nje, pogledao je u oči i rekao samo jedno: „Kate, želiš li mi nešto reći?“

Katarina se počela tresti. Goran se uplašio i nije razumio što joj je, jer je to za njega bilo „normalno pitanje“. Ona ga je, potpuno u šoku, uhvatila za ruku i zamolila da izađu van jer želi razgovarati.

Vani mu je rekla da joj je strašno žao što ga je vrijeđala i ponižavala, da vidi da je dobar čovjek i da gaji simpatiju prema njemu, ali da se bojala njegove prošlosti. Sada je, smatrala je, kasno, jer on odlazi u Njemačku i ima drugu, pa mu želi sve najljepše u životu. Govorila je, prema Goranovim riječima, cijeli sat, dok je on šutio „kao svećenik na ispovijedi“.

Kad je napokon došao do riječi, priznao je istinu: djevojka u Njemačkoj uopće ga ne zanima, zaljubljen je u Katarinu, voli je i želi s njom provesti cijeli život. Katarina se razljutila jer je bila sigurna da odlazi. Goran pak napominje da je, šuteći i slušajući, saznao sve što je trebao znati. „Nekad valja i slušati“, kaže, i dodaje da je znao da mu je to jedina prilika.

Bio je toliko uporan i naporan da je Katarina na kraju zaplakala i nazvala ga lažovom koji ju je prevario. Nakon dugog razmišljanja pristala je: „Dobro. Idemo probati.“ Postavila je i jasan uvjet: **nema seksa, nema poljupca ni u obraz, nema ni držanja za ruku sve do vjenčanja**, „ako bude vjenčanje“. Goran je pristao.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak sadrži vrijedne elemente: Katarina se moli tražeći Božju volju, Goran joj naposljetku priznaje istinu, a njezin uvjet uzdržljivosti do braka jasno izražava želju za čistoćom. Ipak, točno podudaranje unaprijed zadanog pitanja samo po sebi ne dokazuje da je odnos Božja volja, a početna obmana i dugotrajno uvjeravanje ostavljaju pitanje koliko je njezin pristanak bio slobodan od pritiska.
concerns: Katarinin „dogovor“ s Isusom oslanja se na jedan vrlo određen znak; priča ga predstavlja kao potvrdu, ali ne pokazuje dovoljno razloga da se slučajna podudarnost poistovjeti s pouzdanim utvrđivanjem Božje volje.
Goranovo priznanje dolazi nakon što je lažno prikazao odlazak i drugu djevojku. To što je napokon rekao istinu jest bolje od nastavka obmane, ali ne poništava način na koji je izazvao razgovor.

Pristanak nakon dugog nagovaranja i njezina izričita nazivanja Gorana lažovom zahtijevaju oprez: tekst ne omogućuje siguran zaključak da je riječ o prisili, ali treba razlikovati slobodan pristanak od popuštanja zbog emocionalnog pritiska.
magisterium.enrichment: Uzdržljivost prije braka, uključujući dogovorene granice tjelesne nježnosti, dobro se uklapa u katoličko shvaćanje zaruka kao razdoblja priprave i čistoće, a ne kao „pokusnog braka“. Njezina odluka da ne dopusti ni poljubac ni držanje za ruku stroža je osobna granica, a ne univerzalni zahtjev koji ovaj prikaz može nametnuti svim parovima; važno je da se takva granica poštuje i da je odnos istinit i slobodan.

citations.document_author: Catholic Bishops’ Conference of England and Wales

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage contains valuable elements: Katarina prays seeking God's will, Goran ultimately confesses the truth to her, and her condition of abstinence until marriage clearly expresses a desire for chastity. Nevertheless, the exact match of a pre-set question does not in itself prove that the relationship is God's will, and the initial deceit and prolonged persuasion leave open the question of how free her consent was from pressure.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Abstinence before marriage, including agreed boundaries of physical affection, fits well into the Catholic understanding of courtship/betrothal as a period of preparation and chastity, and not as a “trial marriage.” Her decision not to allow even a kiss or holding hands is a stricter personal boundary, and not a universal requirement that this depiction can impose on all couples; it is important that such a boundary be respected and that the relationship be truthful and free.
concerns_en: Katarina's “agreement” with Jesus relies on a single very specific sign; the story presents it as confirmation, but does not provide sufficient reasons to equate a coincidental match with a reliable determination of God's will.

Goran's confession comes after he falsely presented leaving and another girl. The fact that he finally told the truth is better than continuing the deceit, but it does not undo the way he provoked the conversation.

Consent after long persuasion and her explicit calling of Goran a liar warrant caution: the text does not allow a definite conclusion that coercion was involved, but free consent must be distinguished from giving in due to emotional pressure.

sections.subtitle_en: "Do You Want to Tell Me Something?": An Agreement with Jesus on Križevac
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts the moment in the café when he asked Katarina the crucial question
sections.content_en:
Not knowing what to do, Katarina went to **Križevac**. There she knelt under the cross and, as Goran recounts, told Jesus that she was sad because Goran was leaving, that Jesus knew what she felt toward him, but that she did not know whether it was His will for her to open her heart to him. That is why she suggested an "agreement": if Goran that evening of his own accord asked her the exact question **"Do you want to tell me something?"**, that would be a sign of God's will for her and then she would tell him everything.

That evening Goran entered a café for coffee and saw Katarina with two female friends. Immediately he took a chair, sat down next to her, looked her in the eyes, and said only one thing: "Kate, do you want to tell me something?"

Katarina began to shake. Goran became frightened and did not understand what was wrong with her, because for him that was a "normal question." She, completely in shock, took him by the hand and asked to go outside because she wanted to talk.

Outside she told him that she was terribly sorry for having insulted and humiliated him, that she saw he was a good man and had affection for him, but that she was afraid of his past. Now, she considered, it was too late, because he was leaving for Germany and had another woman, so she wished him all the best in life. She spoke, according to Goran's words, for a full hour, while he remained silent "like a priest at confession."

When he finally got a chance to speak, he admitted the truth: he was not interested in the girl in Germany at all, he was in love with Katarina, loved her, and wanted to spend his whole life with her. Katarina got angry because she was sure he was leaving. Goran, on the other hand, notes that by keeping quiet and listening, he learned everything he needed to know. "Sometimes it's good to listen too," he says, and adds that he knew that was his only chance.

He was so persistent and relentless that in the end Katarina wept and called him a liar who had deceived her. After long deliberation she agreed: "Okay. Let's try." She also set a clear condition: **no sex, no kiss even on the cheek, not even holding hands all the way until marriage**, "if there is a marriage." Goran agreed.

sections.subtitle: Ultimatum od dva dana i svećenik iz djetinjstva
sections.screenshot_description: Goran otkriva da je svećenik na Križevcu bio isti onaj iz Katarinina djetinjstva
sections.content:
Uslijedilo je **petnaest mjeseci hodanja**. Goran je stalno požurivao: ima puno godina, želi se oženiti, imati obitelj i djecu i živjeti normalno. Katarina je odgovarala da polako, jer ako se žuri, znači da nešto skriva. Kad mu je, kako kaže, „došlo do ovdje“, posjeo ju je i dao joj **ultimatum: dva dana** da odluči hoće li se udati. Ako neće, neće se ljutiti, ali će svatko krenuti svojim putem. Voli je, ali s njom neće „hodati deset godina okolo“.

Katarina je bila u šoku. S jedne strane ga je voljela i htjela se udati, a s druge je trebala prihvatiti za cijeli život čovjeka s takvom prošlošću, pa je bilo normalno da se boji. Ponovno se uspela na Križevac. Ondje je zatekla skupinu hodočasnika iz Slovačke i među njima svećenika s Biblijom pod rukom. Zamolila ga je da joj je posudi. Jedna žena iz skupine povikala je da joj je da, jer sigurno traži odgovor preko Biblije. Svećenik ju je zamolio da klekne, pomolio se nad njom, blagoslovio je i posudio joj Bibliju.

Pod križem je Katarina iznijela Isusu sve svoje strahove:

- Što ako se Goran ponovno počne drogirati ili opijati?
- Što ako je počne tući?
- Je li brak uopće njezin poziv?
- Kako će ostati živjeti u Međugorju gdje nikoga ne poznaje?

Zatvorenih očiju otvorila je Bibliju i pročitala redak na koji joj je pao pogled: **„Ostani gdje si, to je tvoj put, ne boj se, ja sam s tobom.“** Goran to tumači kao jasno „udaj se za Gorana“. Na njegovo šaljivo negodovanje, Katarina, „kao žena“, ni tada nije bila sigurna. Vratila je Bibliju i krenula niz brdo.

Nakon desetak koraka zastala je, okrenula se i pogledala svećenika. Tada se sjetila. Kad je imala jedanaest i pol godina, sa sjevera Češke išla je na praznike baki na jug. Jednog jutra s bakom je bila na misi koju je slavio mladi svećenik. Nakon mise prišao joj je, zamolio je da klekne, pomolio se nad njom za njezin životni poziv i obećao da će je stalno pratiti molitvama. Dvanaest godina nakon toga nije ga vidjela. **Svećenik na Križevcu bio je upravo on.** Tek je tada Katarina bila sigurna da je to Božja volja.

Goran dodaje da su s tim svećenikom, **ocem Dušanom**, i danas u kontaktu i da ih posjećuje s hodočasnicima. Ističe još jedan detalj: crkva na jugu Češke u kojoj se otac Dušan pomolio nad djevojčicom Katarinom bila je **crkva svetog Jakova**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iskreno prikazuje molitvu i traženje Božjega vodstva, ali otvaranje Biblije nasumce i kasnije prepoznavanje svećenika ne bi trebalo predstavljati kao siguran dokaz da je Bog zapovjedio Katarini da se uda za Gorana. Ultimatum može biti izražavanje osobne granice, no brak zahtijeva slobodan i promišljen pristanak, pa se ne smije donositi pod pritiskom.
concerns: Nasumično otvoren redak može biti poticaj za molitvu, ali sam po sebi nije pouzdana metoda razlučivanja niti jamstvo da se Božja volja izravno očitovala kroz taj redak.

Podudarnost sa svećenikom iz djetinjstva može se doživjeti kao providonosna i ohrabrujuća, ali ne dokazuje sama po sebi da je brak bio Božja volja; razlučivanje uključuje savjest, molitvu i razborito prosuđivanje.
Rok od dva dana može stvoriti emocionalni pritisak. Iz prikaza se ne može zaključiti da je Katarina bila prisiljena ili da je brak nevaljan, ali sloboda izbora supružnika mora biti poštovana.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćansko razlučivanje ne odbacuje osobne znakove ili iskustva, ali ih provjerava u svjetlu vjere, savjesti i razboritosti; osjećaj sigurnosti može biti važan osobni plod, ali nije isto što i dokaz. Katolička tradicija opisuje izbor životnog stanja kao odluku koja traži molitveno razlučivanje, a istodobno brak ne smije biti nametnut izravnom ili neizravnom prisilom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage honestly depicts prayer and seeking God's guidance, but opening the Bible at random and subsequently recognizing a priest should not be presented as definitive proof that God commanded Katarina to marry Goran. An ultimatum can be the expression of a personal boundary, but marriage requires free and deliberate consent, and so must not be made under pressure.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian discernment does not reject personal signs or experiences, but tests them in the light of faith, conscience, and prudence; a feeling of certainty can be an important personal fruit, but it is not the same as proof. Catholic tradition describes the choice of a state of life as a decision requiring prayerful discernment, while at the same time marriage must not be imposed by direct or indirect coercion.
concerns_en: A randomly opened verse can be an impetus for prayer, but in itself is not a reliable method of discernment nor a guarantee that God's will was directly manifested through that verse.

The coincidence involving the priest from childhood can be experienced as providential and encouraging, but does not prove in itself that marriage was God's will; discernment involves conscience, prayer, and prudent judgment.

The two-day deadline can create emotional pressure. From the depiction it cannot be concluded that Katarina was coerced or that the marriage is invalid, but the freedom of choice of spouses must be respected.

sections.subtitle_en: A Two-Day Ultimatum and a Priest from Childhood
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran reveals that the priest on Križevac was the very same one from Katarina's childhood
sections.content_en:
There followed **fifteen months of dating**. Goran was constantly hurrying things: he was getting on in years, wanted to get married, have a family and children, and live normally. Katarina answered to take it slowly, because if one is in a hurry, it means one is hiding something. When, as he says, "it reached up to here," he sat her down and gave her an **ultimatum: two days** to decide whether she would get married. If she wouldn't, he wouldn't be angry, but each would go their separate ways. He loved her, but he wouldn't "date around for ten years" with her.

Katarina was in shock. On the one hand she loved him and wanted to get married, and on the other she had to accept for a lifetime a man with such a past, so it was normal that she was afraid. Once again she climbed Križevac. There she encountered a group of pilgrims from Slovakia and among them a priest with a Bible under his arm. She asked him to lend it to her. A woman from the group shouted to give it to her, because she was surely looking for an answer through the Bible. The priest asked her to kneel, prayed over her, blessed her, and lent her the Bible.

Under the cross Katarina presented all her fears to Jesus:

- What if Goran starts doing drugs or drinking again?
- What if he starts beating her?
- Is marriage her vocation at all?
- How will she remain living in Međugorje where she knows no one?

With closed eyes she opened the Bible and read the verse upon which her eyes fell: **"Remain where you are, that is your path, do not be afraid, I am with you."** Goran interprets that as a clear "marry Goran." To his humorous grumbling, Katarina, "as a woman," was not sure even then. She returned the Bible and started down the hill.

After about ten steps she paused, turned around, and looked at the priest. Then she remembered. When she was eleven and a half years old, she went on holidays from northern Czech Republic to her grandmother in the south. One morning with her grandmother she attended a Mass celebrated by a young priest. After Mass he approached her, asked her to kneel, prayed over her for her life vocation, and promised that he would constantly accompany her with prayers. For twelve years after that she had not seen him. **The priest on Križevac was that very man.** Only then was Katarina certain that this was God's will.

Goran adds that with that priest, **Father Dušan**, they are still in contact today and that he visits them with pilgrims. He points out another detail: the church in the south of the Czech Republic where Father Dušan had prayed over the young girl Katarina was the **Church of Saint James**.

sections.subtitle: Vjenčanje kod svetog Jakova, petero djece i plodovi molitve jedne maćehe
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o maćehi koja je godinama plaćala mise za njegovo obraćenje
sections.content:
Krug se zatvorio **3. lipnja 2000.**, kad su se Goran i Katarina vjenčali u crkvi svetog Jakova, ali ne u Češkoj, nego u Međugorju. Danas imaju **petero djece**: Luciju (18), Luku (15), Anu (13), Marka (9) i maloga Jana (5). Za sve to Goran zahvaljuje i daje slavu Bogu, „nikome drugom“.

Posebnim riječima govori o svojoj **„drugoj mami“**, ženi koju se njegov otac oženio nakon majčine smrti i koju je on nekoć mrzio. Dvaput se, kaže, zbog njega htjela ubiti. Ta je žena svih devet godina koje je proveo na ulici svaki mjesec plaćala svetu misu za njegovo obraćenje. Nikad se nije umorila, nikad nije izgubila nadu i nikad nije prestala vjerovati u njega, iako mu nije bila rođena majka. Svu ljubav koju nije pokazao biološkoj majci, „jer sam bio glup“, danas daje njoj.

Otac mu je još živ i ima 86 godina, a Goran se šali da izgleda bolje od njega. Brat već dugo godina ne pije. Oženio se gluhonijemom ženom i imaju dvije zdrave kćeri.

Na vlastitom primjeru Goran svjedoči i o **ozdravljenju**. Otkako je došao u Međugorje, nikad nije imao napadaj epilepsije. Nestale su i sve paranoje i strahovi, pa se danas, smije se, boji „jedino Boga i svoje žene“. Češka je, dodaje, „opasna kao požar“, ali to mu je dobro.

Liječnici mu nisu davali ni godinu dana života, a prošle se godine napunila **41 godina otkako živi s metkom u glavi**. Priču zaokružuje anegdotom o sinu Luki. Luka mu je jednom rekao da je zaista sretan čovjek. Kad ga je Goran pitao zašto, sin mu je odgovorio: „Tebi nitko ne može reći da nemaš ništa u glavi.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na zahvalnosti Bogu, vjernosti u obiteljskom životu i ustrajnoj molitvi za obraćenje drugoga. Iskustvo prestanka epileptičkih napada i nestanka strahova valja prikazati kao osobno svjedočanstvo, a ne kao dokaz da je potvrđeno čudesno ozdravljenje ili da će se isto dogoditi drugima.
concerns: Tvrdnju o ozdravljenju treba razlikovati od crkvenog utvrđenja čuda: opis svjedoči o Goranovu iskustvu, ali sam ne daje medicinsku ni crkvenu potvrdu uzroka.
Šala da se boji samo Boga i žene očito je izrečena u humorističnom tonu; ipak, izraz straha Božjega u katoličkom smislu označava poštovanje i pokorност Bogu, a ne strah od nasilja.
magisterium.enrichment: Zahvaljivanje Bogu za obitelj, život i dobra primljena kroz druge ljude odgovara biblijskomu pozivu da se u svemu zahvaljuje Bogu. Ustrajna molitva maćehe za Goranovo obraćenje prikazuje molitvu zagovora i nadu koja ne odustaje, ali ne znači da se obraćenje može iznuditi: odgovor druge osobe ostaje slobodan.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Catholic emphasis on gratitude to God, fidelity in family life, and persistent prayer for the conversion of another. The experience of the cessation of epileptic seizures and the disappearance of fears should be presented as personal testimony, rather than as proof that a miraculous healing has been confirmed or that the same will happen to others.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Giving thanks to God for family, life, and the good received through other people corresponds to the biblical call to give thanks to God in everything. The stepmother's persistent prayer for Goran's conversion depicts intercessory prayer and hope that does not give up, but does not mean that conversion can be coerced: the response of the other person remains free.
concerns_en: The claim of healing must be distinguished from the Church's confirmation of a miracle: the description testifies to Goran's experience, but in itself does not provide medical or ecclesial confirmation of the cause.

The joke that he fears only God and his wife was obviously made in a humorous tone; nevertheless, the expression of the fear of God in the Catholic sense signifies reverence and submission to God, not fear of violence.

sections.subtitle_en: Wedding at Saint James, Five Children, and the Fruits of a Stepmother's Prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran speaks about the stepmother who paid for Masses for his conversion for years
sections.content_en:
The circle closed on **June 3, 2000**, when Goran and Katarina were married in the Church of Saint James, but not in the Czech Republic, rather in Međugorje. Today they have **five children**: Lucija (18), Luka (15), Ana (13), Marko (9), and little Jan (5). For all of that Goran gives thanks and gives glory to God, "to no one else."

He speaks with special words about his **"second mom,"** the woman his father married after his mother's death and whom he once hated. Twice, he says, she wanted to kill herself because of him. That woman, for all nine years that he spent on the street, paid every month for a holy Mass for his conversion. She never grew tired, never lost hope, and never stopped believing in him, even though she was not his birth mother. All the love that he had not shown to his biological mother, "because I was stupid," today he gives to her.

His father is still alive and is 86 years old, and Goran jokes that he looks better than he does. His brother has not been drinking for many years. He married a deaf-mute woman and they have two healthy daughters.

Through his own example Goran also witnesses to **healing**. Since he came to Međugorje, he has never had an epileptic seizure. All paranoias and fears also disappeared, so today, he laughs, he fears "only God and his wife." The Czech woman is, he adds, "dangerous as a fire," but that is good for him.

Doctors did not give him even a year of life, and last year marked **41 years since he has been living with a bullet in his head**. He wraps up the story with an anecdote about his son Luka. Luka once told him that he was truly a happy man. When Goran asked him why, his son replied to him: "No one can tell you that you have nothing in your head."

sections.subtitle: Ikone, metadon u kući i jedina preostala napast
sections.screenshot_description: Goran odgovara na pitanje publike o napastima i iskušenju s metadonom
sections.content:
Na kraju svjedočanstva Goran poziva publiku da postavlja pitanja. Na pitanje čime se danas bavi otkriva da je **ikonograf**. Dok je još bio u krizi u zajednici, **sestra Elvira** čula je njegovu priču i rekla momcima da ga, kad kriza prođe, upišu na tečaj pisanja ikona. Objašnjava da onaj tko slika Boga mora biti čist, moliti se i postiti, i smatra da je upravo to bio jedan od načina koji je mnogo pomogao njegovu duhovnom obraćenju i ozdravljenju. Usput se našali da kumu već tri godine duguje jednu ikonu.

Za ikone mu, međutim, sada ostaje malo vremena. Od ožujka do studenog svaki dan održi tri do četiri svjedočanstva. Supruga radi kao vodička s grupama hodočasnika iz Češke i Slovačke. Kad je ona s grupama, Goran čuva djecu i uči s njima, a kad je ona kod kuće, on svjedoči. „Borimo se iz dana u dan“, kaže.

Na pitanje je li nakon ženidbe imao napasti vratiti se na staro, prvo opisuje dalji radni put. Nakon zahoda i metle radio je u **župnom uredu**, gdje je primao narudžbe misa. Ljudi iz Splita koji bi došli platiti misu bježali bi kad bi ga vidjeli, a po Splitu su pričali da je prevario fratre.

Potom su mu fratri predložili posao u **Centru za borbu protiv droge** koji se tek otvarao u Mostaru. Nakon razgovora s policijom i liječnicima primljen je i ondje dugo radio. Obilazio je Mostar, skupljao ovisnike s ulice, oduzimao im heroin, travu i tablete te sve to pred njima bacao u WC školjku.

Jednom su ga u petak navečer nazvali iz **Caritasa** jer im je iz Italije stiglo dvije pune torbe metadona, zamjene za heroin. Goran je te torbe dva i pol dana čuvao u svojoj kući, a **uopće mu nije palo na pamet** da uzme drogu. To pripisuje više Božjoj milosti nego vlastitoj snazi.

Jedina napast koja mu je ostala, priznaje kroz smijeh, jest **pivo uz utakmice**. Kad se u kafiću gleda Liga prvaka ili reprezentacija i svi piju pivo, on pije sok koji više ne može ni vidjeti, pa naručuje kavu za kavom dok ga ne zaboli želudac. Pivo ipak još nije popio. „A i neću. Šta ću sad, sad sam već i star.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkom duhovnošću: molitva, post, borba protiv napasti i zahvalno pripisivanje ozdravljenja Božjoj milosti odgovaraju kršćanskom shvaćanju obraćenja i ljudske ovisnosti o milosti. Govor o ikonama također je načelno spojiv s katoličkom tradicijom, koja dopušta svete slike, ali razlikuje njihovo štovanje od klanjanja koje pripada samo Bogu.
concerns: Tvrdnju da onaj tko slika Boga mora biti čist, moliti i postiti najbolje je razumjeti kao osobni duhovni ideal, a ne kao crkveni uvjet za izradu ikona ili jamstvo njihove valjanosti.
Šala o pivu ne predstavlja naukovni problem, ali katolički nauk ne smatra samo pivo ili umjereno uživanje u piću samo po sebi grijehom; važni su razboritost i izbjegavanje neumjerenosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska askeza, uključujući post, može izražavati obraćenje i usmjeravati osobu prema Kristu, ali je sredstvo duhovnog rasta, ne zasluga koja sama proizvodi ozdravljenje. Katolička tradicija razlikuje štovanje svete slike od klanjanja: slika upućuje na prikazanu osobu, dok se klanjanje iskazuje samo Bogu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic spirituality: prayer, fasting, struggle against temptation, and grateful attribution of healing to God's grace correspond to the Christian understanding of conversion and human dependence on grace. The discourse on icons is also in principle compatible with Catholic tradition, which permits sacred images but distinguishes their veneration from the Eucharistic adoration / adoration that belongs to God alone.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian asceticism, including fasting, can express conversion and direct a person toward Christ, but it is a means of spiritual growth, not merit that of itself produces healing. Catholic tradition distinguishes the veneration of a holy image from adoration: the image directs toward the person depicted, whereas adoration is offered to God alone.
concerns_en: The claim that one who paints God must be pure, pray, and fast is best understood as a personal spiritual ideal, rather than an ecclesial requirement for the creation of icons or a guarantee of their validity.

The joke about beer does not pose a doctrinal problem, but Catholic teaching does not consider beer itself or moderate enjoyment of drink to be inherently sinful; prudence and the avoidance of immoderation are what matter.

sections.subtitle_en: Icons, Methadone in the House, and the Only Remaining Temptation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran answers an audience question about temptations and the trial with methadone
sections.content_en:
At the end of his testimony Goran invites the audience to ask questions. To the question of what he does today, he reveals that he is an **iconographer**. While he was still in withdrawal in the community, **Sister Elvira** heard his story and told the guys to enroll him in an icon writing course when the withdrawal passed. He explains that whoever paints God must be pure, pray, and fast, and he considers that precisely this was one of the ways that greatly helped his spiritual conversion and healing. Along the way he jokes that he has owed an icon to his best man for three years already.

For icons, however, little time remains for him now. From March to November he delivers three to four testimonies every day. His wife works as a tour guide with groups of pilgrims from the Czech Republic and Slovakia. When she is with groups, Goran looks after the children and studies with them, and when she is at home, he gives testimony. "We fight day to day," he says.

To the question of whether after marriage he had temptations to return to his old ways, he first describes his further career path. After the toilets and the broom he worked in the **parish office**, where he took Mass intentions. People from Split who came to pay for a Mass would run away when they saw him, and around Split they talked that he had deceived the friars.

Then the friars suggested to him a job at the **Center for the Fight Against Drugs** that was just opening in Mostar. After an interview with the police and doctors he was accepted and worked there for a long time. He toured Mostar, collected addicts from the street, confiscated heroin, weed, and pills from them, and flushed all of it down the toilet right before their eyes.

Once on a Friday evening they called him from **Caritas** because two full bags of methadone, a heroin substitute, had arrived for them from Italy. Goran kept those bags in his house for two and a half days, and **it did not cross his mind at all** to take the drugs. He attributes that more to God's grace than to his own strength.

The only temptation that remained for him, he admits with laughter, is **beer with matches**. When people watch the Champions League or the national team in a café and everyone is drinking beer, he drinks juice, which he can't even stand the sight of anymore, so he orders coffee after coffee until his stomach hurts. Still, he has not had a beer yet. "And I won't. What am I going to do now, now I'm already old."
